articles.title: Why there are still no non-WebKit browsers on iOS | The Mozilla Blog
articles.summary:
Why there are still no non-WebKit browsers on iOS
Firefox on iPhone is growing fast across the world. This is especially true in the EU since 2024, when the EU Digital Markets Act (DMA) started requiring Apple to let people choose their default browser; millions have picked Firefox, and daily use on iOS has doubled. People want to choose the browser on their phone.
But there remains an important limitation to what is available on iPhones: Apple forces all browsers on iOS to be built on Apple’s own browser engine.
This has meant that companies like Mozilla cannot easily bring the full range of Firefox features and functionality to iPhone users because many of these are built within our browser engine, Gecko. iPhones and iPads are unique in having this restriction. On all other major operating systems, including Apple’s macOS, people can access the Gecko-powered version of Firefox.
As a result of the DMA, Apple began allowing alternative browser engines on iOS in the EU. It published a set of conditions that companies like Mozilla must comply with to bring their own browser engine. At the time we said Apple’s rules made it “as painful as possible” for alternatives like Gecko. In the meantime, Japan also introduced new rules requiring alternative browser engines on iOS. Apple applied very similar conditions in Japan to those in the EU.

articles.title: “Un phénomène nouveau et massif” : pour la présidentielle, les stars de YouTube soumises aux mêmes règles que la télé
articles.summary:
Présidentielle 2027 : HugoDécrypte et les gros youtubeurs devront respecter le pluralisme sous peine de sanctions
L'ARCOM vient de mettre en place de nouvelles règles autour du pluralisme politique pour la campagne présidentielle de 2027. Les créateurs de contenus sont pour la première fois concernés, et cela ne passe pas auprès des intéressés.
Le pluralisme politique est un sujet qui fait déjà couler beaucoup d'encre quand il est question de sa pertinence et de son application à la télévision ou à la radio. Cette obligation de traiter sur un pied d'égalité l'actualité et les interventions de tous les candidats et partis, déjà rarement parfaitement appliquée, va concerner une nouvelle source d'information dans le cadre de l'élection présidentielle de 2027.
Depuis ce 19 novembre 2026, l'ARCOM, le gendarme des numériques qui se refuse toujours à supprimer la chaîne CNews malgré ses nombreux manquements à ses obligations légales, a décidé d'étendre cette règle aux créateurs de contenus et autres influenceurs à partir du 16 mars 2027.
Des gros créateurs de contenus et influenceurs visés par l'ARCOM
L'ARCOM vise principalement les "créateurs dont les audiences dépassent celles de chaînes" selon son président Martin Ajdari, comme Legend ou HugoDécrypte. D'après l'entité, "certains créateurs jouent désormais, dans le débat public, un rôle comparable à celui des chaînes de télévision." articles.title: Andrey Zvyagintsev believes filmmakers know what the audience wants — not executives
articles.summary:
The year is 2022. Vladimir Putin has announced the military draft. In Andrey Zvyagintsev’s Minotaur, set in the fictional town of Krasoborsk, a quietly unhappy couple, called Gleb and Galina, carry on with their lives, or try to, geopolitics notwithstanding. For Galina, carrying on means an affair, which we deduce from a scene of her texting with a faint smile, her face lit in the dark by the light of her phone. (Minotaur is a remake of Claude Chabrol’s 1969 film The Unfaithful Wife, whose title gives the plot away more readily than Zvyagintsev’s.)
Andrey Zvyagintsev believes filmmakers know what the audience wants — not executives
The director of Minotaur says there is no politics in Russia.
Meanwhile, Gleb runs a kind of private contracting concern and is soon asked to scare up military recruits to meet a quota. At this point, the domestic noir and the workplace drama merge to dramatic, devastating, and darkly funny effects.
In Minotaur, as in his five other features, Zvyagintsev has the camera moving seemingly objectively, almost omnisciently, putting the characters in their context. Occasionally they appear rather small, especially when set against the epic scale of their mythic and biblical fates. That the environment shapes the person seems to be a recurring revelation across all six of his staggering films. articles.title: nginx2root: five new nginx vulnerabilities, and how Cloudflare protects origins from the worst of them
articles.summary:
nginx2root: Five new nginx vulnerabilities, and how Cloudflare protects origins from the worst of them
On November 18, 2026, F5 and nginx.org disclosed ten vulnerabilities in nginx. Five of them, detailed by the Xint research team and published under the name nginx2root, are memory corruption flaws that an unauthenticated attacker can use to crash an nginx worker or, per Xint's research, run commands on the server. Xint also found a Linux kernel bug that turns that foothold into root on the host, including from inside a Docker container. Other teams found the two HTTP/2 bugs independently: F5 also credits Rapid7, Wiz Research and Ikotas Labs for CVE-2026-123007, and Metnir, Wiz Research, and Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 for CVE-2026-123633.
nginx is an HTTP web server that also serves as reverse proxy, content cache, load balancer, TCP/UDP proxy server, and mail proxy server. nginx runs a large share of the world's web servers, so this is a patch-now event. But if your nginx server is reachable only through Cloudflare's proxy, attackers cannot reach the vulnerable code paths for the most serious of these bugs, giving you protection while you update your servers.
Here is where Cloudflare stands, what that protection covers, where it stops, and how the bugs work.
The short version

articles.title: « J’aurais un seul regret, celui de ne pas pouvoir tester GTA 6 sur cette TV » : un lecteur de Frandroid raconte son essai du Hisense 75UR9S — Frandroid
articles.summary:
Choisir un téléviseur, c’est aussi imaginer les soirées que l’on va passer devant. Retrouver les décors d’un film, explorer un jeu sur grand écran, lancer une série en pleine journée… Mathias, le lecteur que nous avons recruté pour cette opération en partenariat avec Hisense, comptait bien essayer tout cela. Amateur de belles images, pointu sur le plan technique, il cherchait un téléviseur fluide, avec un bon rendu des couleurs et une jolie luminosité.

articles.title: Votre PC passera-t-il le test ? Windows 11 pourra bientôt bloquer vos applications s’il est jugé mal protégé : voici les conditions
articles.summary:
Chaque application décidera si elle se contente d’un avertissement ou si elle bloque son logiciel.
Le 17 novembre 2026, lors de sa conférence Ignite, Microsoft a présenté Windows Baseline Protection, une fonction qui permettra à Windows 11 d’indiquer à n’importe quelle application si l’ordinateur respecte un socle minimal de sécurité.
L’éditeur de l’application pourra ensuite en tirer les conséquences qu’il souhaite. La fonction est déjà en préversion pour les membres du programme Windows Insider, et son arrivée auprès du grand public est prévue pour 2027.
Les protections à activer
Pour assurer ce suivi, l’outil s’appuie sur des mécanismes déjà présents dans Windows 11, comme la puce TPM, Secure Boot, la sécurité fondée sur la virtualisation ou l’intégrité de la mémoire.
S’y ajoutent des règles sur les pilotes, qui doivent être signés et certifiés, le blocage des pilotes vulnérables, ainsi que la désactivation du mode de signature de test et du débogueur du noyau.
Il suffit qu’une seule de ces protections manque pour que le PC soit déclaré non conforme.
Selon la documentation partagée par l’entreprise américaine, une application pourra obtenir une réponse binaire, la liste des protections manquantes ou, pour les usages sensibles, une attestation cryptographique adossée au matériel, que l’éditeur vérifie sur ses propres serveurs et qui est donc bien plus difficile à falsifier.
Les développeurs choisiront la sanction

articles.title: A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
articles.summary:
A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
Scientists have developed a promising new method that could read quantum information with 99.85% accuracy while barely disturbing the qubit itself.
- Date:
- November 4, 2026
- Source:
- Fundação de Amparo à Pesquisa do Estado de São Paulo
- Summary:
- Researchers have proposed a breakthrough technique for reading quantum information without destroying the delicate states that make quantum computers work. By detecting an electrical signal generated by the qubit itself, their method achieved up to 99.85% accuracy in simulations and could make future quantum computers simpler and more efficient.
- Share:
One of the biggest obstacles in quantum computing is surprisingly simple to describe: how do you read information without changing or destroying it? Unlike the bits used in ordinary computers, quantum bits, or qubits, are extraordinarily sensitive to measurement. Trying to determine their state can cause that state to collapse, potentially erasing the very information scientists want to retrieve.
Researchers have now proposed a way to overcome much of this difficulty by using an unusual electrical signal produced by the qubit itself. Their approach focuses on a special type known as an "Andreev qubit," which can generate an oscillating electric supercurrent through its own quantum behavior. By monitoring this current, scientists may be able to determine the qubit's state without directly measuring it or …

articles.summary:
JPMorgan Chase, Visa and Mastercard have disclosed incidents involving outside service providers after the N0n extortion group claimed it stole their customers’ data.

“Based on our investigation so far, we believe the attackers accessed certain marketing data held by those vendors, which may include some customer names and email addresses. There is no disruption to our services,” the bank said.
Where appropriate, the bank plans to reach out to impacted customers and give them free credit monitoring. It said the incident has nothing to do with the problems some customers saw earlier this week.
In a statement to the media, Visa said the claims are “associated with an incident involving a third-party service provider in Asia Pacific.” The payments giant said neither its own systems nor payment data such as card numbers had been impacted.

Mastercard said its payment network was not affected and that cardholders can still use their cards.

articles.title: Boys Noize turns to the club (and an obscure Italian synth) for inspiration on 7LLVSION
articles.summary:
If you’re wondering how Alex Ridha’s (aka Boys Noize) collaboration with Nine Inch Nails influenced his new record 7LLVSION, the answer is simple: It didn’t. That’s not to say Ridha didn’t learn anything from the virtuosic production team of Trent Reznor and Atticus Ross, but most of the songs on 7LLVSION had been knocking around for some time. And as Ridha is quick to point out, these are not rock songs built for live performance; they’re “battle tested” for clubs and DJ sets. “I was kind of back on the usual kind of thing,” he tells The Verge.
Boys Noize turns to the club (and an obscure Italian synth) for inspiration on 7LLVSION
‘I always look for the newest machines.’
“I do the same I kind of always do. I go make coffee, go in my room, put on the machines, and I’ll start messing around with sounds and build one sound to another and there comes a record,” he says. Like previous Boys Noize releases, a lot of 7LLVSION starts with sound design. “It’s kind of tech-driven, in a way,” he says, “because I always look for the newest machines.”
On 7LLVSION, Ridha frequently turned to an obscure Italian semimodular synth, the Grp A4. “It’s just so powerful, and it sounds so big,” he says. The routing options, dual filters (which he uses in parallel), and built-in sequencer kept leading him to new and inspiring places. Because of that, the A4 ended up on a number of tracks, including “Shut It Down,” “1+1+1,” and “Ycore.”.

articles.title: How Cloudflare WAF helps protect against phpAfterShell and other critical PHP flaws
articles.summary:
How Cloudflare WAF helps protect against phpAfterShell and other critical PHP flaws
On November 19, 2026, the security research company depthfirst disclosed phpAfterShell (CVE-2026-126714), a vulnerability in PHP's default file-based session handler that can lead to remote code execution. Under the Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) 4.0, it scores 9.2 out of 10 (Critical). The PHP project fixed it the same day in versions 8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28, 8.5.13, and 8.6.0. These releases fix 16 other security vulnerabilities, six of them also rated critical.
Cloudflare’s web application firewall (WAF) blocks known phpAfterShell attack patterns, including for customers on the Free plan. The protection comes from a PHP remote code execution rule we first deployed in October 2026 for the php2shell vulnerabilities. That rule already detected part of the phpAfterShell attack pattern before the vulnerability was disclosed, and on November 19 we updated its detection logic to cover phpAfterShell. The rule is part of both the Cloudflare Free Managed Ruleset and the Cloudflare Managed Ruleset, is enabled by default, and its default action is Block.
In the same WAF release, we added three new rules to the Cloudflare Managed Ruleset for paid plans: one for a request smuggling flaw in PHP-FPM (CVE-2026-129289), and two for flaws in PHP's SOAP extension (CVE-2026-15353 and CVE-2026-129506) that PHP fixed in the same releases. articles.title: N-able Blames Service Disruption on Cyberattack
articles.summary:
N-able Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud services experienced a days-long disruption across all regions after hackers compromised one of the company’s servers.
The disruption began on November 16, and N-able initially blamed it on “a combination of platform configuration and service dependencies”.
Mail flow and filtering were not affected, but related services, such as logging, mailbox synchronization, the management portal, and quarantine, were taken offline.
On November 18, the company confirmed that a cyberattack was behind the disruption, noting that it found no evidence that customer data was compromised.
“Our investigation determined that the incident was isolated to a single web server, where an unauthorized party may have been able to access certain credentials stored on the platform,” the company told SecurityWeek.
N-able says its restoration and remediation efforts continue. While inbound and outbound filtering are operating, access to its portal and API remains disabled.
“We took immediate action to contain the incident, including taking the affected server offline, rotating internal platform credentials, revoking existing customer API tokens, invalidating OAuth tokens, and proactively resetting passwords for local users,” N-able said.
The company says its investigation into the incident remains ongoing while it scrambles to securely restore its dashboard and API access.

articles.title: A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
articles.summary:
A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
- Date:
- November 7, 2026
- Source:
- University of Regensburg
- Summary:
- Scientists have discovered a surprising quantum limit that prevents electrons from being tracked with unlimited precision in both space and time. The breakthrough could pave the way for manipulating chemical reactions and developing electronics hundreds of thousands of times faster than today's technology.
- Share:
Quantum physics places fundamental limits on what scientists can know about the behavior of particles. Werner Heisenberg's famous uncertainty principle states that certain properties, such as a particle's position and momentum, cannot both be measured with unlimited precision. This restriction is not caused by flaws in scientific instruments. It is built into the laws of nature.
But position and time are different. Heisenberg's uncertainty principle does not impose the same restriction on these quantities. Now, researchers have experimentally demonstrated another fundamental limitation: an electron's location and its behavior over time cannot both be determined with arbitrary precision. Known as the "space-time limit," this newly observed relationship could have major implications for the future of quantum technology and ultrafast electronics.

The UE series has a sleek lightweight design and combines it with an advanced drivetrain system to deliver comfort and performance without compromise.
The UE series is built for commuting, running errands or enjoying a weekend ride.
The bike has an ultralight 2.35kg carbon fibre frame has a total bike weight of 20.9kg, which means it offers ideal handling for commuting and is easier to load onto trains and elevators.

articles.title: I Don’t Trust Visual Recordings Anymore. But One Day I Will Again
articles.summary:
In March of this year, a flurry of emails and text messages from a half dozen reporters around the world disrupted my quiet Saturday morning. An Iranian news agency had aired a week-old video of what appeared to be a U.S.-made Tomahawk missile hitting a school. News reports claimed that the strike killed more than 175 people, most of them children. The U.S. president and military denied responsibility. In the age of generative AI and all things deepfake, everyone—including me—was skeptical of the video’s authenticity.
I get this type of request a lot. For the past three decades, I’ve been developing mathematical and computational techniques to analyze and detect manipulation in digital media. Over this time, I think it’s fair to say that I, like most people, have approached visual recordings with a “presumption of authenticity”: If a skeptic claims that a recording is fake, the burden of proof is on them.
In today’s world of generative AI, however, I think we need to shift this stance to a “presumption of fake.” That is, the burden is now on the creator to prove that their content is real. While this new stance may seem unfair to legitimate creators, I think it both reflects reality and points to a future where we will once again be able to trust that most online media is what it appears to be.

articles.title: How Cloudflare WAF protects against ruby2shell (CVE-2026-132825)

How Cloudflare WAF protects against ruby2shell (CVE-2026-132825)
On November 19, 2026, the Ruby team disclosed ruby2shell (CVE-2026-132825), a heap buffer overflow in the way Ruby changes the case of strings. Ruby rates the flaw Critical and says it is aware of proofs of concept that achieve remote code execution in some scenarios. Fixes shipped in Ruby 3.3.14, 3.4.13, and 4.0.10.
The reach is wide. Veria Labs reports that Ruby on Rails and classic-style Sinatra applications reach the bug in their default configuration, before any authentication. Self-hosted products that bundle Ruby, including GitLab, GitHub Enterprise Server, Mastodon, OpenProject, Discourse and Chatwoot, shipped an affected Ruby in their latest release at the time of disclosure.
Cloudflare WAF blocks ruby2shell for all customers, including those on the Free plan. We have added two rules to both the Cloudflare Free Managed Ruleset and the Cloudflare Managed Ruleset, with Block as the default action: one for ruby2shell and one for GHSA-87fm-7w84-j2px, a related integer overflow in Ruby string case conversion fixed in the same releases.
The WAF is a compensating control, not a replacement for patching. Exploits can reach the bug through paths a WAF does not see, and the only complete fix is to upgrade Ruby. Our team continues to monitor attack traffic and will update the rules as new techniques appear. articles.title: Ruby Patches Ruby2Shell Vulnerability That Could Lead to RCE
articles.summary:
Fresh security updates for the Ruby programming language resolve seven vulnerabilities in its regular expression engine and in the case conversion of strings. Proof-of-concept (PoC) code demonstrating remote code execution (RCE) exists for five of them.
At the top of the list sits CVE-2026-132825 (CVSS score of 7.4), described as a heap-based buffer overflow in the case conversion of strings that could potentially lead to RCE in certain scenarios.
Dubbed Ruby2Shell, the flaw impacts character case-conversion operations. In some single-byte encodings, including ISO-8859-1 and Windows-1252, when changing the case of a string, Ruby may end up writing one byte past the output buffer.
“For example, converting the German character ß to uppercase produces SS. In affected code, Ruby checks that sufficient space exists for one byte but writes two, potentially corrupting adjacent heap memory,” Previdian explains.
Veria Labs reports that, in default Ruby configurations, unauthenticated attackers could trigger the security defect from Rails, classic-style Sinatra, and potentially other frameworks.
According to preemptive exposure management firm WatchTowr, “any Ruby application that changes the case of external text in a single-byte encoding” is affected by the vulnerability.

articles.title: Claude teria ajudado a resolver um dos maiores enigmas da matemática
articles.summary:
O matemático Levent Alpöge, da Anthropic, afirma ter provado a hipótese de Riemann com a ajuda da inteligência artificial Claude. O problema é considerado um dos mais difíceis e importantes da matemática.
A solução ainda não passou por verificação independente. A alegação surge em meio ao avanço acelerado de sistemas de IA na produção de resultados matemáticos.
Hipótese de Riemann ainda depende de crivo científico
Formulada em 1859, a hipótese de Riemann trata da distribuição dos números primos e da relação entre esses números e os zeros de uma função matemática. Ela integra os sete Problemas do Milênio, administrados pelo Instituto Clay de Matemática, cada um com recompensa de US$ 1 milhão (cerca de R$ 5,7 milhões).
Para que uma solução seja considerada para a premiação, as regras do instituto exigem publicação e pelo menos dois anos de análise, período em que o trabalho precisa receber aceitação geral da comunidade matemática internacional. Desde a criação do prêmio, há 25 anos, apenas a conjectura de Poincaré recebeu reconhecimento oficial como resolvida.
Em documento publicado em seu site, Alpöge afirma que os argumentos foram formalizados sem pressupostos no Lean e que o método também resolve a hipótese generalizada de Riemann. Segundo ele, com mais tempo de trabalho, seria possível avançar até a hipótese estendida.

articles.title: Unos científicos dicen que la materia oscura está compuesta por los elementos de una tabla periódica oscura
articles.summary:
Llevamos muchos años intentando dar una explicación a la materia oscura. Se define así a esa materia invisible, por la que, entre otros fenómenos, las galaxias giran más deprisa de lo que puede provocar la materia visible y la luz se curva a su alrededor más de lo esperado. Hay algo cuya gravedad está provocando estas alteraciones, pero no sabemos qué es. Si bien hay una minoría de científicos que creen que la materia oscura en realidad no existe, la mayoría de ellos coinciden en que, sin ella, no se podría explicar el modelo cosmológico estándar. Pero no consiguen identificarla.
La mayoría de hipótesis apuntan a que está compuesta por un tipo de partícula desconocida, como los WIMPs o los axiones. Sin embargo, un equipo de científicos de Estados Unidos y Canadá considera que eso no es lo que más sentido tiene. Los cálculos apuntan a que en el Universo hay 5 veces más materia oscura que materia convencional. No es una diferencia tan grande para partículas totalmente diferentes. Cinco frente a uno. Por eso, ellos proponen una hipótesis radicalmente distinta, protagonizada por lo que han bautizado como una tabla periódica oscura.
Demasiado similares. Si la materia oscura estuviese compuesta por un solo tipo de partícula, radicalmente distinto a las partículas que componen la materia que conocemos, lo normal sería que la diferencia en la cantidad de un tipo de materia y otro fuese también radicalmente distinto. articles.title: Alerte sur Mars : Perseverance est en panne et son principal relais n'a plus que 2 mois de vie

La Nasa avait déjà perdu la sonde MAVEN en décembre 2025. Cette sonde étudiait l’atmosphère martienne et relayait aussi les données des rovers. En juin 2026, la Nasa a déclarée MAVEN irrécupérable. Désormais, Perseverance a lui aussi un problème de communication. Ce rover a parcouru plus de 42 kilomètres sur Mars, et l’un de ses trajets a même été tracé par l’IA Claude fin 2025.
Or, il ne peut plus utiliser ses deux radios UHF. Ce sont elles qui envoient les gros volumes de données aux sondes en orbite, qui les relaient ensuite vers la Terre. Dans un billet publié ce jeudi 19 novembre 2026, la Nasa explique avoir suspendu toutes les activités scientifiques du rover. Perseverance reste stable et en contact, mais il ne prend plus aucune photo.
Que s’est-il passé sur Perseverance ?
Le 30 octobre, au démarrage, la radio principale n’a pas envoyé ses « battements de cœur », ces signaux réguliers qui prouvent à l’ordinateur de bord qu’elle fonctionne. Après 25 signaux manqués, soit environ 100 secondes de silence, le rover a coupé cette radio. Il est passé sur la radio de secours et s’est mis en mode sans échec (safe mode), où tout ce qui n’est pas essentiel est éteint. Les ingénieurs ont ensuite découvert que la radio de secours n’émettait qu’à la moitié de sa puissance prévue.
Perseverance parle donc directement à la Terre grâce au Deep Space Network, le réseau d’antennes géantes de la Nasa. Mais le débit est bien plus faible, et il est réservé aux diagnostics.

Fue en 1917, en plena Primera Guerra Mundial. El precio fue de 25 millones de dólares en oro. Desde entonces pasaron a llamarse las Islas Vírgenes de Estados Unidos.
El traspaso también afectaba a Santo Tomás, San Juan y Santa Cruz, más los islotes cercanos. Hasta ese momento eran conocidas como las Indias Occidentales Danesas.
Es importante conocer que el sistema económico de estas islas estaba basado en las plantaciones y la compraventa de esclavos. Aunque la esclavitud había sido abolida en 1848, el negocio del azúcar empezó a perder interés.
Según el Museo Nacional de Dinamarca, los barcos daneses llevaron a unas 120.000 personas esclavizadas de África al Caribe. En las islas se basaba el sistema de producción azucarera en mano de obra forzada.
En la historia del archipiélago también hay episodios de resistencia de la población esclavizada. En 1733 hubo una rebelión en San Juan. Se alzaron contra el dominio danés. En el reglamento del gobernador Philip Gardelin se detallan algunos de los castigos extremos que se practicaron.

Las carreteras, por ejemplo.
Unas cajas azules. Nos lo cuentan nuestros compañeros franceses de L'Automobile, los conductores de su país empiezan a preguntarse qué son esas cajas azules que están junto a la carretera y si deberían o no tener algo en cuenta. La respuesta más obvia es que se trata de un radar (en Francia tienen todavía más experiencia que en España en este sentido). Pero no, no es un radar.
Las cajas azules son los nuevos postes para cobrar un peaje a los vehículos de más de 3,5 toneladas a partir de abril de 2027. Es lo que se llama Ecocontribución y sólo lo pagarán los camiones que superen dicho peso, quedando exentos los vehículos de particulares y, evidentemente, las motocicletas.

Arma nuclear poderia atingir satélites em diferentes órbitas
O desenvolvimento russo contraria o Tratado do Espaço Exterior de 1967, acordo das Nações Unidas que proíbe a colocação de armas nucleares e outros armamentos de destruição em massa em órbita terrestre.
De acordo com a DIA, uma detonação nuclear poderia ser direcionada a satélites em diferentes altitudes. Isso inclui equipamentos em órbita baixa, usados em atividades comerciais e de reconhecimento; em órbita geoestacionária, importante para comunicações; e em órbita média, onde operam satélites de navegação e sincronização de tempo.
O relatório também aponta outras ameaças espaciais desenvolvidas por China e Rússia, como mísseis antissatélite, ataques cibernéticos, interferência eletrônica e armas de energia direcionada.

articles.title: F5 releases emergency patches for critical BIG-IP RCE flaws
articles.summary:
US cybersecurity company F5 warned customers to patch five BIG-IP vulnerabilities that attackers can exploit to trigger denial-of-service (DoS) or gain remote code execution.
Tracked as CVE-2026-121805, CVE-2026-120292, CVE-2026-120285, CVE-2026-116953, and CVE-2026-123637, these stack-based buffer overflow flaws affect the company's BIG-IP Access Policy Manager (APM) centralized access management proxy solution and the BIG-IP iRules programmable scripting feature.
All five security issues are rated critical severity, and unauthenticated threat actors can exploit them to terminate the Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM) and execute arbitrary code remotely on systems with vulnerable configurations.
The company also released engineering hotfixes for a high-severity BIG-IP APM SAML vulnerability (CVE-2026-126822) stemming from an integer underflow (wrap or wraparound) weakness that remote, unauthenticated threat actors can abuse in denial-of-service (DoS) attacks.
"Traffic is disrupted while the TMM process restarts. This vulnerability allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the BIG-IP system and may perform RCE," F5 said. "There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only."
F5 said it has no mitigation measures for these flaws and advised security teams to install the out-of-band hotfixes released on Wednesday to address them on vulnerable devices.

More than 300,000 people in the United States die from sudden cardiac arrest each year. This deadly emergency occurs when the heart's electrical system suddenly fails, causing the heart to stop pumping blood. It can strike older adults with known heart conditions as well as seemingly healthy young athletes. A partir de ahí la vista no vuelve atrás al guardar el teléfono ni al bajarse del coche. El método lo detalló por primera vez un hilo de r/GTA.
Con costuras. Nada de esto es oficial, y se nota. Es completamente jugable, pero está sin acabar: los hombros del personaje se cuelan en el plano al empuñar un arma grande y la animación de forzar un coche es muy tosca. Quantum computers are getting too powerful to check. Scientists have a solution
- Date:
- November 16, 2026
- Source:
- University of Innsbruck
- Summary:
- Scientists have developed a new way to determine whether quantum simulations can be trusted, solving a growing problem as quantum computers become too powerful for conventional machines to check. Demonstrated on a 51-qubit system, the technique measures uncertainty and provides verifiable error margins that could help unlock the full potential of quantum computing.
- Share:
As quantum computers grow more powerful, researchers face a troubling question: How can they know whether the results are correct when conventional computers can no longer verify them? Scientists have now developed a promising new method that could help overcome this challenge by measuring the accuracy of quantum simulations and identifying how much uncertainty their predictions contain.
The technique uses experimental measurements to reconstruct how a quantum system behaves, then calculates how uncertainties in that reconstruction affect the results. Researchers successfully demonstrated the approach using a quantum simulator with up to 51 qubits in Innsbruck, Austria.

articles.title: Lumepay's Huang uses stablecoins to simplify African cross-border payments
articles.summary:
For Harry Huang, the problem with moving money across borders was not something he discovered in a boardroom or at a fintech conference. He had seen it much earlier, through his family’s import-export business.
His parents were building a business in South Africa, dealing with suppliers and customers beyond the country’s borders. But making international payments was not always as simple as instructing a bank to transfer money. Sometimes it required personal connections, patience and navigating exchange rates that did not match what businesses expected.
“Sometimes, you had to find someone who knew someone just to get a payment done,” Huang said in an interview with TechCabal on Monday. “It wasn’t as straightforward as going to a bank. The exchange rates were also different from what you would see on Google or other platforms.”
For businesses trying to trade across borders, these are more than administrative frustrations. Delayed payments, unpredictable foreign exchange costs and difficulty moving money can determine whether a company pursues an opportunity in another market or walks away from it.
Huang believes he can help address some of those problems. As co-founder and chief executive officer (CEO) of South African fintech Lumepay, he is building cross-border payment infrastructure that combines traditional banking systems with stablecoin technology to help businesses collect, convert and move money across African markets.

Android ha caminado por una senda que cruza multitud de territorios. El open source, el código propietario, dispositivos de múltiples formatos y hasta adaptaciones a móviles de la competencia, ya que hay maneras de usar Android en iOS. Esta capacidad de disfrazarse es una de sus cualidades: la comunidad lleva casi desde el principio modificando el sistema operativo. Y esto se encuentra en peligro de extinción.
Las ROMs, en retirada. No es que hayan desaparecido, ya que colosos como LineageOS siguen en plena forma. Lo que sí es cierto es que pasaron a un público muy especializado, aquel que no tiene miedo de modificar su smartphone a fondo. Yo mismo hace tiempo que dejé de ser uno de ellos.
He pasado de visitar a diario los repositorios de ROMs a no acordarme ni del root. Sé que es solo mi experiencia, pero las cifras van en la misma línea: en una encuesta del medio especializado Android Authority, la mayoría de lectores declaraba que su móvil no estaba rooteado. Y eso que hablamos del público más aficionado. En el conjunto de Android, la proporción es mínima: LineageOS tiene 1,6 millones de instalaciones activas frente a los más de 3.800 millones de usuarios Android activos. Menos del 0,1%.

La ley de crédito inmobiliario diferencia entre ventas vinculadas y ventas combinadas. En las primeras no se ofrece la posibilidad de contratar el préstamo de manera independiente (el préstamo está en el paquete). Las ventas vinculadas están prohibidas (salvo excepciones legales). En las ventas combinadas sí se ofrece la posibilidad de contratar el préstamo por separado. En este caso hay que informar de las diferencias y costes de cada producto.

articles.summary:
There are 146 companies listed on the Nigerian Exchange (NGX), a number the bourse wants to double as it works towards a $1 trillion market capitalisation over the next decade.
“We are looking forward to all the founders here to take advantage of our platform to also increase that number,” Jude Chiemeka, chief executive officer of the NGX, said at the Lagos launch of the AT50 Index on Wednesday. “We do have a very strong ambition to double that number in the near term. The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) capital market plan aims to raise the equity capital market to $1 trillion in the next 10 years.”
Nigeria’s equity market closed at $117.11 billion on Thursday, a fraction of the Johannesburg Stock Exchange’s (JSE) approximately $1.35 trillion market capitalisation. South Africa’s exchange represents the scale Nigeria hopes to achieve.
Nigeria’s stock market has jumped 61.31% since January 2, when it had a market capitalisation of $72.6 billion. That means its value has almost doubled in roughly 11 months, reflecting a strong rally in Nigerian equities. If the market sustains annual growth of 30%, it could cross the $1 trillion mark in roughly nine years, reaching approximately $1.24 trillion by November 2035.
But sustaining this pace will require more companies entering the market, more capital being raised, and a broader pool of investors willing to finance businesses listed on the exchange.
This is where technology companies become important to the NGX’s ambition.…

articles.title: N-able says recent security breach led to major service outage
articles.summary:
N-able says attackers who breached one of its servers have caused a major outage affecting Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud services worldwide.
On Tuesday, the company initially blamed the outage on what it described as a "combination of platform configuration and service dependencies" affecting Mail Assure and SpamExperts services across the Americas, Asia-Pacific, and Europe.
However, one day later, N-able disabled UI and API access and confirmed unauthorized access to a server in the Hosted Cloud environment.
N-able also said the cyberattack didn't affect email flow or spam filtering and that it has yet to find evidence that the attackers gained access to customers' data and mailboxes.
"Our earlier update said the disruption came from platform configuration and service dependencies and we believed we had remediated the issue. As we continued our investigation, we determined that the disruption was caused by a security incident affecting the Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud environment," the company said.
"We are aware of unauthorized access to one of the servers in the Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud. We have taken steps to mitigate the threat and are continuing to harden our services to reduce the risk of recurrence. The investigation is ongoing, but at this time we do not have evidence that customer data was compromised, including access to tenants' mailboxes."

articles.title: Le directeur technique de Ledger annonce son départ après neuf ans
articles.summary:
Charles Guillemet, le directeur technique de Ledger, quittera le fabricant français de portefeuilles crypto à la fin de l’année. Il annonce son départ alors que plusieurs clients de la marque ont perdu leurs cryptos avec des appareils piégés et une fausse application.
Charles Guillemet a officialisé son départ sur son compte X, et il reconnaît que ces mots sont « étranges à écrire » après neuf ans chez Ledger. Le dirigeant assure que l’entreprise ne sera pas prise de court. « Nous préparons cette transition depuis de nombreux mois, les équipes, les partenaires et les feuilles de route de Ledger sont donc prêts », écrit-il. Il quitte son poste au milieu d’une série d’attaques contre les clients du fabricant, dont certains avaient acheté leur portefeuille, trafiqué à leur insu, chez un revendeur.
Charles Guillemet a bâti la sécurité de Ledger à partir de rien
Il est entré chez Ledger en décembre 2017 au poste de directeur de la sécurité, « sans bureau, sans équipe », raconte-t-il. Il crée alors le Donjon, le laboratoire d’attaque du fabricant. Ses chercheurs tentent de percer les défenses des appareils avant les pirates, et ils ont signalé des failles dans tout le secteur des cryptomonnaies. L’équipe a notamment contourné le démarrage sécurisé de smartphones, cette protection qui vérifie que le logiciel lancé à l’allumage n’a pas été modifié. articles.title: Does your AI agent need an LLM to decide what to do next?
articles.summary:
Does your AI agent need an LLM to decide what to do next?
Say “good morning” to an AI agent, and it might search its long-term memory before saying hello back. Somewhere in that system, a service performs a semantic lookup to determine whether your greeting requires understanding your beverage preferences. Even if you take your coffee very seriously, this seems like a lot of infrastructure for two words.
Does this request need a more capable model than conventional options? Is this retrieved memory relevant? Should the workflow pause for a human?
This inefficiency and indecision is where Mike Chambers, a senior AI DevEx engineer at AWS, sees an opportunity. In a conversation last month at AGNTCon + MCPCon North America 2026 in San Jose, California, Chambers explained to The New Stack Editor-in-Chief Nick Lucchesi how developers can use decider models to handle the small judgments that add up inside an agent.
Decider models (also called decision models or System One models) are specialized AI models that choose from a fixed set of options or rate inputs on a scale — returning calibrated probabilities without generating free-form text. Popularized by TypeSafe AI’s Jev, they give software and agentic workflows fast, low-latency judgments with explicit confidence scores. (AWS’s Strands Labs released its own open-source decision model, the 2-billion-parameter Strands Decider 2B, on October 1.)

articles.title: Anthropic says Claude writes and reviews 90% of its team's code. The catch is how it checks the work.
articles.summary:
Anthropic says Claude writes and reviews 90% of its team’s code. The catch is how it checks the work.
Anthropic says Claude writes and reviews roughly 90% of the code produced by the team building Claude Code, and the company has spelled out how it verifies that work without making engineers inspect every change.
In a Monday engineering post, Anthropic technical staff member Addy Osmani describes a verification system built to support dozens or even hundreds of concurrent agents, where automated checks supply the evidence engineers need to judge what those agents produce.
The approach has attracted scrutiny from developers, much of it centered on the cost of model-driven verification and whether cheaper deterministic tooling could shoulder some of that load instead.
In response to questions from The New Stack, Anthropic walked through how it controls inference costs, stops agents from manipulating tests, and gauges whether its automated reviewers actually work.
Testing AI code live
The company has Claude exercise its changes inside a running application, leaning on browser automation for web apps, MCP-connected simulators for mobile builds, and local services for backend work.
Those instructions live in repository-specific verification skills under .claude/skills/, so an agent can run and check its own changes before it ever commits them.

articles.title: The most misunderstood graph in AI just got a major update
articles.summary:
The most misunderstood graph in AI just got a major update
METR’s latest report finds that AI models are still improving at a rapid clip, but they show some weaknesses in tasks that require judgment.
A new report from the AI evaluation nonprofit METR finds that some AI capabilities are continuing to improve along an exponential trajectory—but it also indicates that models aren’t quite as good at tasks that require judgment as they are at coding.
The report is an update to the organization’s time horizon plot, which was widely shared—and widely misinterpreted, owing to the complexity of the measures it used. METR evaluated models by having them attempt a large suite of tasks, each of which had also been completed by humans. Each task’s difficulty was scored by how long it took the human testers to finish it—and then models were rated according to the length of the tasks that they could complete. That plot showed that AI systems were rapidly improving—every four months, the length of the tasks that frontier models could successfully complete doubled.
The updated plot adds more tasks—some that are estimated to take humans far longer than those in the original suite, and others that are more open-ended. One of the biggest questions in AI right now is the extent to which progress on “verifiable” tasks—where it’s possible to check automatically whether an AI system has succeeded or failed—carry over into tasks on which success or failure is harder to measure. articles.title: Redditor forced to bring desktop PC in checked luggage on US-to-UK flight with GPU still installed — GPU stayed installed and tempered glass didn't shatter
articles.summary:
Redditor forced to bring desktop PC in checked luggage on US-to-UK flight with GPU still installed — GPU stayed installed and tempered glass didn't shatter
They even left their GPU and cooler attached during the trip.
A Redditor from the UK was flying from the United States with their desktop PC in a carry-on but was forced to check it. According to u/FattyLeopold, they’ve carried their PC as a carry-on on different flights, and they brought it with them in the cabin all the way across the Atlantic. The trip even included a layover.
“It was 4am, and I was pissed off,” the Redditor replied to one comment. “Just said fu-- it, let’s see what happens. Probably confused the universe a bit, ‘Dude… what are you doing… Aight, have it your way.’” They then taped the PC, monitor, and keyboard together in the package.
The desktop PC only had a bag and several layers of protective wrapping for protection. What’s more surprising is that the owner didn’t even take the GPU off its bracket and put it in their carry-on. When they arrived at their destination, they recorded the “unboxing” of their PC. Against all odds, their computer arrived without a single dent or scratch — the tempered glass on the side of the PC didn’t even shatter after the possible trauma it went through in baggage handling.

An eight-year study of children in Finland has revealed a surprising connection between screen time and brain function. articles.title: Entenda por que o Sul é a região mais propícia à formação de supercélulas
articles.summary:
Uma combinação de fatores geográficos e atmosféricos faz com que a região Sul seja a mais propícia à formação de supercélulas no Brasil. Segundo a Climatempo, a posição dos três estados favorece o encontro de massas de ar com características diferentes, criando condições para tempestades capazes de provocar ventos acima de 90 km/h, granizo e até tornados.
O fenômeno voltou a chamar atenção nesta sexta-feira (20), depois que uma tempestade atingiu Tupanciretã, no Rio Grande do Sul. A Defesa Civil estadual apontou preliminarmente a ocorrência de ventos severos associados a uma supercélula, possivelmente provocados por uma microexplosão. A possibilidade de tornado não foi totalmente descartada.
Por que o Sul favorece essas tempestades?
Um dos principais fatores é o encontro de massas de ar. O Sul costuma receber primeiro e com maior intensidade o ar frio de origem polar. Ao mesmo tempo, correntes de vento transportam ar quente e úmido de áreas mais ao norte do continente.
Quando essas massas se encontram em uma atmosfera com bastante umidade, o contraste de temperatura pode favorecer a instabilidade e o desenvolvimento de grandes nuvens de tempestade.
As supercélulas são estruturas que crescem tanto horizontalmente quanto verticalmente. Entre os fenômenos associados a elas estão rajadas de vento acima de 90 km/h, chuva intensa em pouco tempo, granizo, microexplosões e tornados.

articles.title: WhatsApp Fixes Flaw Uncovered While Disrupting Scam Campaign
articles.summary:
WhatsApp has patched a low-impact vulnerability in its Android apps that it believes a scammer may have exploited to make scam messages seem more credible.
Tracked as CVE-2026-23871, WhatsApp’s security team found the flaw. It’s tied to Click to WhatsApp ads and affects both WhatsApp and WhatsApp Business for Android.
“Incomplete validation of external ad-reply URLs in WhatsApp for Android and WhatsApp Business for Android before 2.26.17.4 could have caused a target’s device to reveal its IP information to an attacker if an attacker sent media from an attacker-controlled URL when a crafted Click to WhatsApp ad-reply message was rendered and displayed in a message thread,” WhatsApp explained in its advisory.
The advisory also says the vulnerability “may have been abused in conjunction with specific spam messages.”
Asked by SecurityWeek about the exploitation, a WhatsApp spokesperson said, “Our team found this issue while disrupting a scam campaign, and we believe a scammer was using it to make their scam message seem more credible.”
WhatsApp also published advisories for two medium-impact vulnerabilities, saying it has seen no evidence that either was exploited.
One of them, CVE-2026-102769, is an SQL injection bug affecting WhatsApp for Android versions prior to 2.26.35.74. Tapping a maliciously crafted “order details” message sent from an unofficial client could lead to the deletion of WhatsApp files stored on the device.

articles.title: Your AI agent’s “memory problem” may be something else
articles.summary:
Your AI agent’s “memory problem” may be something else
An agent may need additional context to continue when a user returns the next day. A workflow may resume from the wrong step, or a preference may be remembered without its scope, or a retrieval may return an outdated document.
These are often described as “memory problems,” but they have different causes. Long-running agents rely on three kinds of context: workflow state to resume execution, durable information to carry across sessions, and external knowledge for the current request. Each needs a clear owner, lifecycle, and access boundary.
LangGraph and LangChain give developers useful abstractions, but the application still needs to define ownership, lifecycle, and access boundaries for each context type. Keeping those responsibilities explicit makes failures easier to diagnose and long-running agents easier to operate.
| Layer | What it answers | What changes over time | 
|---|---|---|
| Workflow state | Where the current run stopped | Nodes, tool results, approvals, pending work | 
| Agent memory | What should be remembered for later | Facts, preferences, decisions, procedures, validity | 
| RAG knowledge | What external evidence supports this request | Documents, chunks, embeddings, versions, access scope | 
A checkpoint can resume a workflow, but it cannot define memory
A workflow checkpoint answers a narrow question: Where should this run continue?

articles.title: AWS Releases a Free Local Emulator of AWS Built Entirely by Agents
articles.summary:
AWS has released AWS Emulator, a free local implementation of more than 200 of its services dedicated to the public domain under CC0, and says that "thousands of autonomous AI agents wrote every line of code" in it. As InfoQ reported at launch, it ships as a single Rust binary generated from AWS's 438 public API models and listens on port 9297. The week since has brought the first independent fidelity numbers and a divided practitioner reaction.
Pointing an existing SDK, CLI, or coding agent at the emulator is a matter of environment variables, after which the launch post by Daniel Abib says, "your existing tests, CLI scripts, and coding agents keep working the way they already do":

articles.title: The ex-banker connecting 2,000 Kenyan farms
articles.summary:
The trouble with arriving 15 minutes late to see Cherotich Rutto, Tawi Fresh founder and chief executive, is that she has the air of a strict school principal who would have noticed at minute one. That is before she says a word. It’s raining on Wednesday when I climb the stairs to her office, one flight above the working floor of the agritech’s godown in Tilisi, a mixed-use development 24 kilometres west of Nairobi.
We first met in Copenhagen in August, where she was speaking about climate innovation and resilient food systems. In Tilisi, she tells me about the sausages her grandmother, a nursery school teacher who raised her and her sister in Nairobi’s Lang’ata, could afford at the end of the month. There was also fresh produce from Taita Taveta, where her grandmother came from. She taught Rutto to pay attention to where her food came from.
“Banking came to me,” she says. She had studied economics and figured she would sell bank products for three months while she waited for an economist’s job. One month became another, and she went on to hold roles at Barclays and Standard Chartered Bank.
By the time she was pregnant with her first child, she and her husband were making weekend trips to their farm in Nanyuki. They put their savings into it and imagined handing it down to their children. When things went badly, they talked about it for the whole three-hour drive home. They lost money, but those weekends helped shape Tawi Fresh, which now supplies hotels, restaurants, schools…

articles.title: On ne verra jamais les scènes coupées de L’Odyssée
articles.summary:
Pour adapter un récit dense comme celui de L’Odyssée, Christopher Nolan a forcément dû faire des choix forts, au moment d’écrire et de tourner, mais aussi au moment de monter. Beaucoup de scènes ont ainsi fini à la poubelle, certaines avant d’être immortalisées, et on ne les verra jamais, pas même en bonus de l’édition Blu-ray.
Car Christopher Nolan a un avis assez ferme sur les scènes supprimées et les différentes versions d’un même film. À ses yeux, la seule et unique édition valable est celle diffusée dans les cinémas. Ce qui revient à dire qu’un montage Director’s Cut, agrémenté de quelques minutes supplémentaires, ne trouve pas grâce auprès de lui.
Christopher Nolan ne veut pas entendre parler d’un Director’s Cut de L’Odyssée
Dans un entretien accordé au média britannique The Independent, publié ce mercredi 18 novembre pour la sortie du film en vidéo, Christopher Nolan assume d’avoir sacrifié des scènes de L’Odyssée : « Il y a beaucoup de scènes coupées chiffonnées au fond de la corbeille à papier que personne ne verra jamais. Je ne crois pas vraiment aux director’s cuts. Je veux assumer le film tel qu’il sort en salle. En tant que scénariste-réalisateur, j’essaie de faire ce travail d’écrémage en amont. Il n’y a pas beaucoup de scènes [coupées] qui ont été tournées. »
Il ajoute : « Sur un film comme celui-ci, passer une journée à tourner quelque chose au sommet d’une montagne, sous la pluie ou sur un bateau, et qui ne figurera finalement pas dans le film, je préférerais…

articles.title: En 1945, la Segunda Guerra Mundial llegó a su fin. Para 286 españoles, la salida no llegó hasta 11 años después en un barco de la Cruz Roja
articles.summary:
La Segunda Guerra Mundial terminó oficialmente en Europa el 8 de mayo de 1945. Para millones de personas fue el principio del regreso a casa, pero hubo españoles para los que la paz no significó la libertad. Algunos siguieron encerrados en campos soviéticos durante años, atrapados entre una guerra que había terminado y otra, la Guerra Fría, que acababa de comenzar. Su historia desembocó en abril de 1954, cuando un barco apareció en Barcelona con 286 compatriotas a bordo.
Los españoles para los que la guerra no acabó hasta 1954. Cuando Alemania capituló, cientos de españoles seguían retenidos en la Unión Soviética. Buena parte pertenecía a la División Azul, la unidad de voluntarios enviada por Franco en 1941 para combatir junto al ejército de Hitler contra Stalin, pese a que España se mantenía oficialmente fuera de la Segunda Guerra Mundial. Otros eran republicanos que habían llegado a territorio soviético durante la Guerra Civil española y terminaron detenidos por las autoridades comunistas.
Mientras Europa intentaba reconstruirse, estos hombres permanecían dispersos por cárceles y campos de trabajo. Nueve años después del final de la contienda, el 2 de abril de 1954, 286 españoles desembarcarían en Barcelona a bordo del Semíramis. Para algunos, la espera había comenzado incluso antes de que terminara la Guerra Civil.

articles.title: Juan José Ebenezer, mecánico: "Por no hacer un mantenimiento cuando corresponde hemos roto el motor, pero cuando digo roto, es caput"

Una de ellas es la correa auxiliar, y descuidar su estado puede acabar saliendo muy caro, justo lo que explica el mecánico Juan José Ebenezer en uno de sus vídeos al señalar cómo una avería que podía haberse evitado terminó dañando el motor de un vehículo.
Ebenezer enseña una correa auxiliar deteriorada hasta romperse y reveló por qué el problema viene después: los restos acabaron entrando en el sistema de distribución, y según el mecánico esto pasa con mucha frecuencia. Así, en lugar de tener una sustitución relativamente sencilla, te topará con una reparación mucho más complicada.
¿Qué puedes hacer en estos casos?
Cuando esos fragmentos llegan a la distribución, pueden impedir que los piñones encajen correctamente y provocar que el sistema pierda su sincronización. Eso es lo que el mecánico describe en el vehículo que está examinando, donde las válvulas han terminado chocando con los pistones. Para comprobar el alcance del problema, intenta girar el cigüeñal, pero descubre que el motor está completamente bloqueado. “Lo tenemos duro como un taco, esto ya ni quien lo mueva”, explica.

articles.title: Still tracking company passwords in spreadsheets? You’re flying blind.
articles.summary:
The password spreadsheet your admins use may look like a complete inventory, but it only reflects some of the credentials employees have reported using. More specifically, that spreadsheet doesn’t show passwords that have been changed, created, or shared since the document was last updated, until someone brings it up to date. That’s assuming someone ever does.
Meanwhile, work passwords can end up in all kinds of places. Someone saves one in their browser.
A teammate sends a shared login in chat to move forward with a project. Another employee decides to put a few passwords in a personal vault because getting access to the company one takes too long.
Unless someone reports these actions, the spreadsheet won’t capture them.
And so, admins may think they have a handle on company credentials when, in fact, their spreadsheet tells only part of the story.
The real reason credentials slip out of admins’ view
The predominant factor is convenience. When the approved process is slow or unclear, employees use what’s at hand: a browser’s built-in password storage, a shared Google document, a Slack message, or one of the sticky notes on their desk.
They may know that that’s against the rules, but in the moment, their priority is getting work done.

Sridhar Vembu warns that a possible US immigration policy reversal could restore population-driven demand in housing and other sectors.
Zoho Co-founder Sridhar Vembu says a political shift in Washington could revive immigration-driven demand in the US economy, including in housing.
In a post on X, he argues that tighter immigration controls reduced a source of demand supporting asset prices, and that a change of course could restore it.
“Given the scale of MAGA losses, it is likely that immigration policy will make a sharp reversal in America, both legal and illegal immigration,” Vembu wrote. He added, “The unsustainable financial and economic bubble had long been sustained with demographic fuel. A good example is housing.”
Vembu said, “The demographic fuel tap for the bubble was shut for a period and now it may be turned back on.” He described this as a possible scenario rather than a firm prediction.
His reference is to the November 3 midterm elections, in which Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress, dealing U.S. President Donald Trump a major political setback. The result could constrain his agenda but does not guarantee an immigration policy reversal. The administration retains control of federal enforcement, while Congress can shape funding and legislation.

articles.title: Canada to appoint US-based Financial Data Exchange to set technical standards for open banking | BetaKit

The federal government has selected a globally recognized, US-based organization to set the technical standard for its forthcoming open banking system, taking another step towards long-awaited financial data portability in Canada.
“The role of the Canada Council is to be putting Canadians in the driver’s seat with full decision-making power.”
Kevin Feltes, FDX
The Department of Finance is set to announce on Friday that Financial Data Exchange (FDX) will serve as Canada’s open banking technical standards body, governing how financial institutions and FinTech companies will securely share Canadians’ data when requested. FDX is US-based, but the non-profit organization has established a “Canada Council” that will have the power to make decisions separate from the FDX board. Voting membership on the Council will be limited to Canadian residents and businesses, according to documents viewed by BetaKit.
The feds are also appointing the Ombudsman for Banking Services and Investments (OBSI) as a designated external complaints body for open banking, where consumers will be able to direct concerns. Since 2023, the organization has also served as the external complaints body for banks.
Founded in the US, FDX has established the most commonly used financial data-sharing standard in North America. In 2020, it launched in Canada with an FDX Canada Working Group, including banks such as Bank of Montreal and CIBC, as well as FinTech companies like Koho and Flinks.

“We are not querying like humans anymore”: OpenSearch’s Bianca Lewis on why AI agent mistakes look like successes
This situation is more common than one might think: An AI agent calls the wrong API, gets a perfectly good response, and carries on as if everything went according to plan. Somewhere a dashboard is still green. For developers used to troubleshooting applications by looking for failed requests, that’s an awkward kind of success.
“In the agentic AI era, we are not querying like humans anymore,” said Bianca Lewis, executive director of the OpenSearch Software Foundation.
In a conversation with The New Stack senior editor for AI Frederic Lardinois at AGNTCon + MCPCon North America 2026 in San Jose, Lewis explained what that shift means for OpenSearch, the open-source project many developers already know from application search or log analytics.
Lewis sees a role for it on both sides of an agent’s work, helping it find the information it needs while enabling developers to see what it did with that same information.
Follow the agent’s trail
Lewis remembers when a failure at least had the decency to announce itself.
“Error 500 queries used to be the best thing that could ever happen because we would know that [something] went wrong,” she told TNS. “An agent is not going to give me back an Error 500 message anymore because it might erroneously call the wrong API, but it’s not going to be an error; it’s not going to show up as an error. South African startup SEQFLO has launched a digital trust platform that adds identity verification, protected payments and dispute resolution to private transactions between strangers.
Founded in Cape Town by Jarrett Booysen, SEQFLO is not a marketplace, but rather acts as a trust and transaction layer for deals that start elsewhere, whether on Facebook Marketplace, Gumtree, WhatsApp, Instagram or a seller’s own website.
Sellers create a transaction on SEQFLO and then advertise through their usual channels. Both parties are verified and agree on the terms before any money changes hands. The buyer then pays through SEQFLO, and the funds are held within the platform’s approved banking and payment structure.
Delivery or collection can be documented with photographs, and the seller is paid once the agreed conditions have been met. If something goes wrong, a structured evidence and dispute-resolution process kicks in.
“We’re not asking people to trust strangers more. We’re building SEQFLO so they don’t have to rely on trust alone,” said Booysen, who built the platform after being scammed himself.
“We constantly tell people to check a profile, ask for ID, look at proof of payment and trust their gut. But sophisticated scammers know exactly how to create those signals of legitimacy,” he said.
SEQFLO is designed to protect both sides of a deal. Buyers are covered against paying for goods that never arrive. Sellers are covered against fake proofs of payment and fraudulent buyers.

The story investors are hearing is a simple one: Anthropic passed OpenAI because it sold to businesses, while OpenAI chased consumers. Tech investor Dan Niles, for example, wrote on the day of the IPO that Anthropic was “focused on day one on enterprises who are willing to pay,” while OpenAI focused on consumers used to getting internet services for free.
For the most part, this is correct. In the twelve months to September 2026, customers paying Anthropic more than $100,000 a year accounted for 74% of its revenue, with the remaining 26% coming from roughly 40 million smaller customers. OpenAI, by contrast, entered 2026 with about 60% of its revenue coming from consumers.
B2C vs B2B…and B2D
Why is Anthropic winning enterprise customers over OpenAI? IMHO, model quality alone doesn’t explain the gap. On broad benchmarks, the two labs’ top models trade places within a point or two, and Anthropic’s edge in coding is real but narrow.

White House national cyber director Sean Cairncross will be stepping down from his role, Axios reported. The news comes as Democrats prepare to take control of Congress and as businesses across the country report a flurry of technical outages whose cause remains unknown.

Since then, he has met with top AI leaders and helped the Trump administration make key AI decisions, according to Axios. The outlet also reports that the split between Cairncross and the White House was amicable, and his departure was timed so that the White House could nab a Senate confirmation for his role before Democrats take control of Congress in January.
Cairncross, a lawyer and longtime Republican operative, had no cybersecurity background when the Senate confirmed him 59–35. He previously served as the Republican National Committee’s chief operating officer and, during Trump’s first term, as CEO of the Millennium Challenge Corporation, a federal foreign aid agency. The office hasn’t been around long; Congress created it in early 2021, and Cairncross was only its third Senate-confirmed director. The first director, Chris Inglis, left after about 19 months, and the job then went about 10 months without a permanent director.
We’ve reached out to the White House for comment.

Key Takeaways
- A 99.99 percent SLA is a statistic, not a promise. Design for the tail of that distribution, because at sufficient scale you will eventually land in it.
- An alert that wakes a human only speeds up notification. Resilience comes from automation that acts on the signal and informs humans afterward.
- A passive region that has never carried production traffic is an untested hypothesis. Active-active keeps both regions continuously validated under real load.
- DNS TTL can nullify a perfectly executed failover. Choose it deliberately against your RTO, health-check interval, and false-positive tolerance, rather than accepting the module's default.
- Faster detection only sharpens the post-mortem timeline. Reliability requires automated recovery plus a confirmation loop that verifies the failover actually worked.

The tech giant is warning customers via pop-ups that if it becomes law, they could face increased delivery costs of up to five dollars per order.
The Delivery Protection Act, also known as Intro 518, would change whose name appears on an Amazon driver's paycheck. Today, the person who drops off your package might wear an Amazon vest, drive an Amazon van, and even have one of Amazon's AI-powered cameras watching how they drive. Their employer, however, is often one of the small businesses Amazon calls Delivery Service Partners.
Under the New York bill, if Amazon wants to keep running its delivery stations in the five boroughs, it would have to put the drivers who regularly deliver packages from those stations on its own payroll. That includes part-timers who do more than eight hours of delivery work in any 30-day period. The rule would also cover workers who sort packages at the stations.
There's a provision for the drivers already doing those jobs. If Amazon ends a delivery contract to comply with the law and its partner lays off the drivers as a result, it would have to offer those drivers their old jobs as Amazon employees before it could hire anyone else to do the work. The terms of those offers would have to be at least as good as the ones the drivers had before.

articles.title: QCon San Francisco 2026: The Future of Apache Iceberg
articles.summary:
Apache Iceberg V4 proposes a redesign of table metadata to improve scalability and support more frequent writes, alongside new capabilities for data management and schema evolution. Daniel Weeks, co-creator of Apache Iceberg and member of technical staff at Databricks, presented a session at QCon San Francisco on the fourth version of the Apache Iceberg open table format specification.
Iceberg V4 will address the limitations of managing very large tables while expanding the format to support new data types and workloads. The speaker described the new version as a major reimagining of the table format rather than an incremental step, with changes including a new metadata tree, more efficient commits, typed column statistics, relative file paths, and support for file and vector data types. While earlier versions left most of the metadata structure intact, V4 addresses problems that emerge at large scale and adds support for new use cases. Weeks told the audience in San Francisco:
V4 is a major reimagining of a table format. We didn't get everything right in V3 and prior, so now we're taking the opportunity to fix some of the biggest things that are challenges as we scale up to even larger data sets and we bring on new use cases.
Apache Iceberg is an open table format for managing large analytical datasets across different data processing engines. Originally developed at Netflix in 2017, it was open-sourced in 2018 and became an Apache top-level project in 2020. The main alterna…

articles.title: Behind Jensen Huang’s exit, questions about a management style reportedly built on fear | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Earlier this week at the DealBook conference in New York, Elon Musk, beamed in from a trip to China with President Donald Trump, was asked about the ouster of his longtime friend, former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Musk compared it to kicking Michael Jordan off the Chicago Bulls’ roster during his historic run. Of Nvidia’s employees, he said, “They love [Huang]. They love him.”
Well, maybe not all of them. Thousands of employees have signed a letter asking for Huang’s return, but others tell The New York Times he ruled through praise and fear, as well as by humiliating people.
According to the Times, Huang told subordinates that Nvidia’s wealth meant it wasn’t possible to motivate employees with money, so humiliation was the only lever left. He reportedly told one executive his mother should have aborted him and told another employee he would rip his arms off and beat him to death with them.
Naturally, over a 33-year career, regrettable things may have been said, but the Times found a long paper trail that suggests the incidents weren’t isolated. In 2005, for example, Michael Winston, a former HR chief, threatened to sue and called Huang’s conduct the most abusive he’d seen. Nvidia paid him more than $1 million. Huang’s spokesman calls the allegations fabrications.

VMware tells users to patch critical security flaws now — vCenter issues could let hackers grab access to your systems
Broadcom issued a fix for five flaws, including a critical-severity one
- Broadcom patched a critical VMware vCenter authentication-bypass flaw that can grant attackers administrative access
- Researchers linked active exploitation to a China-aligned threat group targeting internet-facing infrastructure
- Organizations are urged to patch immediately, as compromise of vCenter can provide broad control over virtualized environments
Broadcom has released an emergency update for VMware vCenter Server to patch a critical-severity vulnerability apparently being used in the wild by cybercriminals associated with the Chinese government.
The company has issued a security advisory covering five vulnerabilities: an authentication bypass in VMware Directory service in vCenter, three issues in SDDC Manager (SQL injection, authenticated command injection, local privilege escalation), and a SAML token signature bypass in VMware Tools for Windows.
“The vCenter issue permits an attacker with network access to vCenter to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access to the system,” the advisory explains. “You are affected if you are running any version of VMware vCenter.”
Exploited in the wild
The vulnerability is tracked as CVE-2026-123890, and was given a severity score of 9.8/10 (critical). It was patched on November 19 2026, and Broadcom now advises everyone to apply …

articles.title: Power and cooling limits push 100,000+ accelerator AI clusters past single data centers — Google, Cisco, and Marvell target ‘scale-across’ networking across regions
articles.summary:
Power and cooling limits force AI clusters with 100,000+ accelerators to use multiple data centers — Google, Cisco, and Marvell target ‘scale-across’ networking across regions
And software gains importance for such distributed data centers.
The rapid growth of AI clusters is pushing computing infrastructure beyond the physical and power limitations of individual data centers, which creates demand for new networking architectures capable of connecting compute resources across multiple facilities and even geographical regions. At Supercomputing 2026 (SC26), researchers from The Ohio State University discussed the evolution of high-performance networking technologies. At the conference, they explained how efficient distributed computing at such a scale requires considerably more than faster network connections, highlighting the importance of scale across domains to stretch workloads across different data centers in separate geographical regions.
Massive systems call for new interconnects
Modern AI clusters typically accommodate more than 100,000 AI accelerators and potentially millions of CPU endpoints, placing tremendous demands on network bandwidth, latency, and congestion management. Meanwhile, an accelerator's computational performance continues to increase faster than communication capabilities, which means that faster AI GPUs do not necessarily deliver proportional improvements in application performance. articles.title: Hackers use autonomous AI tool Cairn to find zero-day, take over server
articles.summary:
Hackers used an autonomous AI agent platform called "Cairn" to discover a zero-day vulnerability in a medical imaging application and exploit it to take complete control of a server.
According to Amazon Threat Intelligence, the suspected Chinese-linked attackers simply instructed the AI agents to "obtain shell access," leaving them to independently discover and exploit the flaw.
Amazon Threat Intelligence uncovered the campaign after discovering that the attackers had left their Cairn instance publicly accessible without authentication, exposing their hacking operations.
According to the researchers, the attacks were launched by a Chinese-nexus threat actor between September 8 and 10, 2026, targeting mainly East Asian educational institutions outside China.
Cairn is a legitimate pentesting tool that can be used to coordinate multiple AI agents in cyber-operations, created for research and defense strengthening.
Gambit Security documented cases of Cairn abuse as part of a large-scale credit card stealing operation in September. More recently, Google reported it was deployed in an attack against an aerospace organization in the U.S.
During the campaign investigated by Amazon, the AI agents were not always successful. For example, a 16-hour and 148-action effort to take control of a Redis server failed.
In a separate case targeting a university GPU server, the agents tried over 30,000 credential combinations over six hours but failed to brute-force their way in.

articles.title: Si vous êtes chez Mullvad, pensez à vérifier votre DNS
articles.summary:
Mullvad demande à ses utilisateurs français de revoir leurs réglages DNS parce que le fournisseur Quad9 cessera de fonctionner dans le pays le 24 novembre. Sans modification, certains sites risquent de ne plus s’afficher.
Depuis la version 16.0, Mullvad Browser envoie les requêtes DNS de ses utilisateurs à Quad9, sauf réglage personnalisé. Mullvad a récemment publié un avis pour expliquer quoi changer.
Changer de DNS, couper le DoH ou passer par le VPN
L’annuaire DNS permet de traduire le nom d’un site en adresse joignable par un appareil. Quad9 est un service gratuit géré par une fondation suisse à but non lucratif. Le service permet aussi de bloquer les domaines liés au phishing et aux logiciels malveillants. Mullvad Browser lui envoie ces requêtes en DNS over HTTPS (DoH), autrement dit chiffrées.
Nous rapportions en septembre que Mullvad fermait ses propres DNS publics chiffrés le 2 novembre. L’entreprise jugeait que faire tourner son propre résolveur doublonnait le travail de Quad9, une fondation spécialisée qui demande des moyens et des compétences. Mullvad préférait donc consacrer ces ressources au financement de la fondation suisse. Nous apprenions le mois dernier Quad9 allait quitter la France. La fondation refusait de bloquer des sites de streaming pirates visés par beIN Sports et avait écopé d’une astreinte de 1000 euros par jour. Elle a fait appel de cette décision. Eazeebox co-founder Srinivas Shanbhogue passes away
Shanbhogue spent two decades at Schneider Electric before building Eazeebox, a Bengaluru startup that helps neighbourhood electrical shops restock from multiple brands through a single app.
Srinivas Shanbhogue, co-founder and CEO of Eazeebox, has died, his former Schneider Electric colleague Bidisha Nagaraj said in a LinkedIn tribute.
Shanbhogue worked at Schneider Electric for 20 years, serving as vice president of home and distribution in India.
In a farewell post in 2023, he recalled coming from a small town and credited Schneider with giving him the opportunity to grow into a business leader. As he left to become an entrepreneur, he told colleagues he hoped to keep contributing to Schneider’s growth from outside the company.
At Eazeebox, Shanbhogue stayed close to the trade he knew from Schneider Electric. A shopkeeper who needs to restock wires, switches and circuit breakers may have to call several distributors. Eazeebox lets retailers order across brands through one app. The startup stocks products in local warehouses and says it can deliver within two hours, with no minimum order size. Shopkeepers can order a few items as they run out.
