articles.title: La escasez mundial de placas de circuitos amenaza la producción de autos, equipos médicos y de defensa
articles.summary:
La industria electrónica mundial enfrenta una escasez de placas de circuitos impresos, los componentes sobre los que se sueldan los chips en casi cualquier aparato. La Global Electronics Association, gremio del sector, emitió el 18 de noviembre una alerta: la falta de suministro afecta a fabricantes de autos, equipos médicos, defensa y telecomunicaciones.
Según la asociación, esas empresas informan plazos de entrega más largos y dificultades para conseguir placas, porque la inteligencia artificial absorbe la capacidad disponible. El gremio sostiene que el riesgo principal no es el precio sino la disponibilidad, y que la situación puede rivalizar con la escasez de chips de 2021.
Los datos de la propia asociación muestran el desfase: entre septiembre de 2025 y septiembre de 2026, los pedidos de placas subieron 56,1%, mientras que los envíos crecieron 13,3%. Para las placas de muchas capas, los plazos de entrega son de 16 a 20 semanas o más.
Los servidores de IA consumen más materiales
Una placa de computadora común tiene unas 12 capas. Las de los servidores de IA pasan a tener entre 40 y 60 o más, y cada capa adicional requiere más tela de fibra de vidrio, resina, lámina de cobre y laminado, según la alerta. Esos materiales también escasean, de modo que ampliar fábricas no basta.

articles.title: How Standard Bank Group automates AI risk assessment for generative AI | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
How Standard Bank Group automates AI risk assessment for generative AI
This post is co-written with Tala Qraitem from AWS and Jörg Fischer from Standard Bank Group
Having an AI policy is one thing. Proving, one use case at a time, that AI systems follow it is another. Every new generative AI application adds one more system to prove. Teams can now build one in days, but each still needs a risk committee’s approval before it reaches customers or employees. When that approval depends on reviewers reading documents and testing the system by hand, governance becomes the slowest step in the pipeline.
Standard Bank Group chose to automate that proof. Working with AWS Professional Services, the bank deployed an automated assessment that scores each generative AI use case against international AI standards and its own policies. The assessment produces reports and a dashboard that show what is already in place, what is working well, and what still needs mitigation. This post explains how the assessment runs on AWS and what Standard Bank Group learned from its first runs.
Governing AI with the framework you already have
Standard Bank Group didn’t need a new AI policy. Like most large banks, it already had an established model risk practice that covers concerns such as explainability and fairness, and a change risk process that assesses each new use case according to its level of risk before it goes live.

articles.title: Un Graal des maths vacille : un chercheur d'Anthropic revendique avoir résolu l'hypothèse de Riemann avec l'IA Claude
articles.summary:
« Je crois avoir, en travaillant avec Claude, découvert une preuve de l’hypothèse de Riemann ». Levent Alpöge, mathématicien salarié d’Anthropic, écrit ces mots dès la première page d’une note de quatre pages mise en ligne ce vendredi 20 novembre sur son site personnel. Si elle tient, cette preuve règle une question restée ouverte depuis 167 ans, avec l’aide de l’IA de son propre employeur.
Bernhard Riemann a formulé son hypothèse en 1859. Elle décrit la façon dont les nombres premiers se répartissent, et une bonne partie de la théorie des nombres part du principe qu’elle est vraie, sans que personne ait réussi à la démontrer. Elle fait partie des sept problèmes du millénaire, dotés chacun d’un million de dollars (environ 910 000 euros) par l’institut Clay.
Alpöge ajoute que sa méthode règle aussi l’hypothèse de Riemann généralisée, qui étend la question à toute une famille de fonctions. Il attribue surtout à Claude les étapes décisives de la fin. Près de la ligne d’arrivée, écrit-il, l’IA l’a « largement distancé », avant, a-t-il ajouté sur un ton plus poétique, de « voler, danser et scintiller ».
Une preuve que personne n’a encore relue
Alpöge n’a publié aucun article scientifique pour exposer sa démonstration. Il a seulement mis en ligne le code de sa preuve, découpé en quatorze archives et écrit en Lean, un langage qui permet à un ordinateur de vérifier chaque étape d’une démonstration.

Facepalm: Security researchers recently discovered a peculiar cybersecurity incident involving POS systems using outdated Microsoft software. The operation relied on an old Windows bug and repurposed publicly available proof-of-concept exploit code, significantly increasing the risk of financial fraud for a large number of unsuspecting cardholders.
Unknown cybercriminals spent months or even years harvesting critical data about millions of credit card transactions on point-of-sale (POS) systems. The operation was eventually discovered because the crew left a server exposed to public access. After breaking in, security researchers found a massive trove of revealing data, including malware source code and details about how the operation came about.
The main culprit behind the malicious operation was a security vulnerability affecting several versions of Windows 10, 11, and Windows Server. Tracked as CVE-2024-49138, this Windows Common Log File System Driver Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability could be exploited to gain SYSTEM-level privileges on a vulnerable Windows system
The CVE-2024-49138 vulnerability, which had a CVSS base score of 7.8 out of 10, was reportedly fixed by a patch Microsoft released in December 2024 for all affected Windows versions. But the cybercriminals were still able to exploit the flaw and compromise over 700 POS machines using the Windows operating system. Esas consultas suelen aterrizar en interrogantes puntuales, como en dónde se celebra la fecha, por qué se eligió el 19 de noviembre y si existe otra fecha asociada a esta conmemoración, como el 19 de marzo. El fenómeno no responde a una casualidad del algoritmo, sino al comportamiento real de los usuarios que buscan entender el origen y el alcance de esta efeméride mundial.
El buscador no inventa preguntas al azar. Las construye a partir de patrones de búsqueda reales, es decir, de las dudas que la gente ya planteó antes sobre el mismo tema.
En el caso del Día Internacional del Hombre, esas dudas se repiten con un patrón identificable: primero se quiere saber la fecha exacta, luego el lugar donde se celebra y, después, el motivo detrás de la elección del día.
Por qué el 19 de noviembre se celebra el Día del Hombre
El Día Internacional del Hombre se celebra el 19 de noviembre porque así lo estableció en 1999 el profesor Jerome Teelucksingh, de la Universidad de las Indias Occidentales, en Trinidad y Tobago, quien eligió esa fecha en homenaje al cumpleaños de su padre y a un hito futbolístico de su país ocurrido en 1989.

articles.summary:
Strom aus dem Kaktus: Forschende zapfen Feigenkakteen 0,5 Volt ab – wofür das gut ist
Feigenkakteen lassen sich als kleine Stromquelle nutzen. Ein Forschungsteam der University of California Santa Cruz hat eine Methode entwickelt, um den Pflanzen geringe Mengen elektrischer Energie zu entnehmen. Die Spannung entsteht in den Stängeln der Kakteen – als Nebeneffekt einer besonders wassersparenden Form der Photosynthese, die die Pflanzen vornehmen. Nutzen ließe sich der Strom laut den Forschenden in der Landwirtschaft, etwa für Sensoren. Die Ergebnisse stehen in einer Studie im Fachmagazin Plants, People, Planet. Beteiligt waren Studierende aus den Ingenieur-, Natur- und Sozialwissenschaften der Hochschule.
Warum Kakteen nachts Kohlendioxid sammeln
Feigenkakteen nutzen den sogenannten Crassulaceen-Säurestoffwechsel, kurz CAM. Dieser Stoffwechselweg hilft der Pflanze, Wasser zu speichern und so in heißen, sonnigen und trockenen Regionen zu überleben. Die Kakteen wandeln Kohlendioxid über 24 Stunden hinweg in Zucker um und nutzen dafür die kühlen Nachttemperaturen. Gewöhnliche Pflanzen gehen anders vor: Sie nehmen Kohlendioxid nur tagsüber unter Lichteinfluss auf. Dazu öffnen sie winzige Poren in ihren Blättern. Durch diese Öffnungen verlieren sie Wasser – für einen Kaktus wäre das kontraproduktiv.

Google has announced it is donating Agent Substrate and gVisor to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF), placing two important components of its AI agent infrastructure under vendor-neutral open-source governance. The move is intended to address two emerging challenges in running autonomous agents at scale: securely executing untrusted, AI-generated code and managing the substantial compute overhead created by agents that frequently pause and resume.
The announcement also includes OpenRL, Google's open-source reinforcement learning orchestration project. Together, the projects target different layers of agent infrastructure, from isolated code execution to managing agent lifecycles and coordinating large-scale training workloads. The goal is to establish an open foundation for agentic applications, much as Kubernetes helped standardise container orchestration.
Google argues that conventional Kubernetes workloads and AI agents have fundamentally different execution patterns.
A traditional application typically starts, serves requests, and continues running. An AI agent, however, may execute a tool or code for a few seconds before waiting for model inference, an external API, or human approval. Google estimates that agents can spend 90-95% of their time idle while still holding important state, including memory, files, repositories, and active sessions.

articles.title: Muchas empresas firman el paro a un trabajador que se marcha voluntariamente: el SEPE tiene un mensaje para ellos
articles.summary:
El trabajador sale de la empresa. Ha acumulado cotización suficiente para poder acceder al paro, pero por el tipo de salida no tiene derecho. Entonces puede pedir que la empresa “arregle los papeles”. Es decir, que conste que su salida fue un despido.
El SEPE advierte que no puede ser la empresa quien otorgue este derecho. Es preciso que conste la verdadera causa de cese. Incluso en caso de baja voluntaria, ha de remitirse el certificado de empresa al SEPE. El problema surge cuando se pretende maquillar los hechos para que parezca un despido y así poder acceder a la indebida prestación.
Qué ocurre si se pacta un despido ficticio
No hay derecho a indemnización por despido en caso de dimisión ordinaria. Sin embargo, sí han de liquidarse las cantidades pendientes (salario, pagas extras…) en el finiquito. Del mismo modo, no hay derecho a indemnización en caso de despido disciplinario procedente, pero si se pacta de mutuo acuerdo un simulacro con tal de poder acceder al paro, es fraudulento.
Esta colaboración para obtener prestaciones indebidas está tipificada como infracción muy grave (Ley sobre Infracciones y Sanciones en el Orden Social). Al beneficiario se le sanciona con la extinción del paro; se le reclama la devolución de la cantidad indebidamente percibida e incluso puede quedar excluido del acceso a prestaciones económicas y algunas ayudas un año.

In den vergangenen Monaten gab es immer wieder Sicherheitsvorfälle bei OpenAI und anderen KI‑Unternehmen. DraftKings notes that its “licensed sportsbook” operates in other states but “not in Florida.”
Multiple companies, including DraftKings, claim that their “swaps” (a type of financial derivative) are, in fact, properly governed by a federal agency, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission. Therefore, DraftKings argues, states cannot regulate this activity as gambling.

In addition, a large order may no longer be enough to secure production capacity at the Taiwanese giant, as the company is reportedly reviewing customers' finances and asking for cash on orders that exceed a set credit limit. Together, the two changes make chips more expensive to build and alter who gets to build them first.
Taiwanese IC design firms have started receiving notices of the increases, with the higher foundry costs expected to take effect in the first quarter of 2027. If design houses cannot pass them on, their gross margins could drop by 4 to 5 percentage points.
Finished products take time to move through the supply chain, so the higher costs should show up in shipments around March or April. Companies are trying to settle new prices with their own customers before April so they do not have to absorb the difference.
The pressure goes well beyond TSMC. TrendForce, which forecasts foundry price increases of 5% to 20% next year, points to rising manufacturing costs and capacity kept tight by AI and server demand. The research firm expects the sharpest increases for 8-inch wafers, while 12-inch pricing will vary by process node.

articles.summary:
El fiscal general de California, Rob Bonta, notificó este 19 de noviembre una citación de investigación a Nvidia. La fiscalía quiere saber si chips avanzados o información confidencial de la empresa llegaron a China y si la compañía engañó a los inversores y al público sobre ese riesgo.
La citación llega una semana después de la renuncia de Jensen Huang, cofundador y director ejecutivo de Nvidia, tras conocerse que tuvo una relación extramatrimonial con Alice Huang. Según CNBC, ella no tiene parentesco con él, es sospechosa de espiar para China y fue ejecutiva de Megaspeed, una empresa de Singapur investigada por un posible desvío de chips restringidos hacia ese país.
Bonta dijo en el comunicado de su oficina que la conducta de Nvidia y de su exdirector ejecutivo “plantea señales de alarma graves”, entre ellas la forma en que la empresa pudo haber engañado a los inversores. “Las empresas no pueden engañar a sus inversores”, afirmó, y definió el caso como una situación “compleja y transnacional” para la compañía.
El fiscal explicó a Politico que la citación es el primer paso de la investigación. Según el comunicado, la información que reciba servirá para evaluar si Nvidia violó las leyes de California, en particular las normas de valores que regulan lo que una empresa cotizada puede decir a quienes invierten en ella.

articles.title: Uber Cuts Translation Cache Memory by up to 90% While Keeping P99 Latency Below 1 MS
articles.summary:
Uber has redesigned its Go-based translation cache to reduce its initial memory footprint by more than 90% while keeping p99 cache miss latency below one millisecond. The hybrid architecture retains translation keys and frequently accessed values in memory while storing the remaining values on disk. The system serves millions of translations per second and maintains a cache hit rate above 99.9%.
The optimization addresses two problems identified through memory profiling across Uber's Go services. Garbage collection (GC) consumed more than 20% of CPU utilization in some services, with translations accounting for approximately 70% of allocated objects.
Uber Engineering noted that
At Uber's scale, even small inefficiencies in memory management can add up.
The first optimization replaced Go's sync.Map with a conventional map[string]string protected by an RWMutex. The workload was predominantly read-heavy, with infrequent updates and no individual deletions. The previous implementation created multiple objects and pointers for each translation entry, increasing GC overhead. Moving to a value-based map reduced object allocations and improved CPU utilization by more than 30% in the affected service.
However, reducing object allocations did not solve the overall memory consumption problem. Translation datasets could contain two to three million keys, although individual services typically accessed only a small subset. Cache refreshes introduced another issue: the service built a repl…

articles.title: Comment El Niño bouleverse le climat : les explications d'un climatologue en vidéo
articles.summary:
L’océan Pacifique tropical traverse une phase de fortes perturbations. Pour mieux comprendre ce qui se joue actuellement à l’échelle de la planète, l’océanographe et climatologue Éric Guilyardi, chercheur au CNRS, apporte un éclairage scientifique rigoureux.
Dans un entretien accordé à Numerama, l’expert revient sur les mécanismes profonds de cette anomalie thermique. Découvrez notre vidéo complète sur YouTube pour saisir l’ampleur de ce phénomène.
El Niño : le fonctionnement d’une anomalie thermique planétaire
Contrairement aux idées reçues, El Niño n’est pas une simple tempête passagère. Il s’agit d’une perturbation climatique majeure s’étendant sur environ un an, causée par un couplage complexe entre l’océan et l’atmosphère. En période normale, les alizés poussent les eaux chaudes vers l’ouest, notamment vers l’Indonésie, ce qui provoque des remontées d’eaux froides à l’est, au large du Pérou. Mais certaines années, ces vents faiblissent, bloquant la remontée d’eau froide et provoquant une surchauffe anormale de l’océan. Pour approfondir ces bases scientifiques, vous pouvez consulter notre dossier détaillant le fonctionnement complexe du phénomène El Niño.
Ce dérèglement cyclique, qui revient tous les 2 à 7 ans, est documenté par les populations locales depuis des générations. articles.title: Google a trouvé la fusée idéale pour envoyer ses puces IA dans l'espace
articles.summary:
Destinées d’abord à la recherche, les puces IA que Google veut envoyer en orbite pourraient permettre par la suite de créer de vrais datacenters dans l’espace. Le projet est prévu pour le premier trimestre 2029 et Google a choisi la fusée qui les enverra : New Glenn, conçue par Blue Origin.
En 2029, Blue Origin enverra des puces Google dans l’espace
Blue Origin et Google annoncent conjointement avoir signé un contrat de services de lancement pour cette première mission lourde dédiée au Project Suncatcher. La fusée New Glenn de Blue Origin devra donc déployer les satellites dans une orbite héliosynchrone (soit environ à 650 kilomètres d’altitude). Cette trajectoire permet de recevoir de la lumière solaire quasiment en permanence, ce qui sera nécessaire pour alimenter les puces d’IA. Blue Origin paraît d’ailleurs confiant sur sa capacité à remplir cette mission, quelques mois après l’explosion d’une fusée New Glenn lors d’un essai.
Car à l’intérieur de ces satellites, il y aura effectivement des puces d’IA Tensor Processing Unit, développées par Google. Chaque satellite devrait avoir une capacité de calcul comparable à celle d’une baie de serveurs de datacenters. Tous ces satellites seront reliés entre eux pour fonctionner de pair et créer un réseau orbital. Dans leur communiqué respectif, ni Google ni Blue Origin n’ont précisé combien de satellites seraient envoyés. Mais le document de recherche de Google publié l’année dernière parlait de 81 satellites.

articles.title: Steam Machine could get even more expensive as Valve warns of rising memory costs
articles.summary:
In a nutshell: Most people believe the Steam Machine costs too much for the performance it offers. Now, around five months after it launched, Valve has hinted that its prices could be changing: they might become even more expensive.
Like pretty much all consumer devices, the Steam Machine has been impacted by the AI-driven memory crisis. Demand for the living room PC has been so high that Valve has only just fulfilled all reservations for the 512GB model. There's finally some stock left over, too, meaning you can buy one now without waiting.
Unfortunately, there's some bad news. Valve says it's still building Steam Machines, but "memory and storage costs continue to increase at unprecedented levels." As a result, the company can't say how many more machines it can make or what it'll charge for them – more probably. It expects to have new information to share in January.
The Steam Machine launched at $1,049 for the 512GB model and $1,349 for the 2TB version, both without a controller. That extra $300 buys you more storage, but you're still getting the same six-core Zen 4 CPU, RDNA 3 graphics with 8GB of VRAM, and 16GB of system memory.
Those prices reflect what Valve paid for components in the six months leading up to launch. The company said it was already selling the Steam Machine at cost, which leaves it little room to absorb another jump in RAM and SSD prices. Spione im Smarthome: Wie Hacker deinen Saugroboter aus der Ferne kapern können

Mit anderen Worten: ein hochinteressantes Angriffsziel.

articles.title: Chips can survive the space environment — can their financing? | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
The push to build data centers in space faces plenty of obstacles, from tricky engineering to a dearth of rockets that could take chips to orbit. But what about paying for the chips?
The data center ecosystem currently depends on debt financing, with cloud providers borrowing to build out data centers and then paying back the loans with a share of the revenue.
Those deals typically use the chips as collateral — if the data centers default on their loans, the lenders can take possession of the chips and resell them. That backstop makes it cheaper for companies to finance their chips. Even older chips retain value — according to Compute Credit Index Research, some H100s are selling for about half of their original cost basis from 2023, while some H200 configurations are selling for the same price they did when introduced in 2024.
But you’re not going to repossess chips installed in a satellite orbiting 300 miles above Earth at 17,500 miles per hour. The Financial Times is reporting that lenders behind SpaceX’s $40 billion chip financing deal asked that none of the chips purchased be used for the company’s orbital data center plans. It’s not clear if they succeeded in getting SpaceX to agree with the provision.
That may not matter to the company in the near term — SpaceX’s ability to deploy compute at terrestrial ground stations has proven lucrative, and on the company’s most recent earnings call, CEO Elon Musk detailed how he was dispatching engineers from the company’s rocket …

articles.title: Meta TLX, a Native GPU Compiler Extension Supporting Advanced Hardware Capabilities
articles.summary:
Meta developed Triton Low-Level Extensions (TLX), designed to bridge the gap between high-level GPU programming abstractions and the low-level execution control required to fully exploit modern GPU architectures.
According to Meta engineers, modern GPU architectures offer advanced performance-optimization features, including warp specialization, asynchronous memory movement, tensor memory, and cluster-level execution, which depart from Triton's traditional programming model, which simplifies kernel development but abstracts away low-level execution structures.
For example, a modern FlashAttention kernel may dedicate one warp group to issuing TMA transfers while another executes tensor-core computation. A Blackwell GEMM kernel may coordinate multiple warp groups, TMEM allocations, and cluster resources simultaneously. In both cases, performance depends not only on the computation being performed, but also on how multiple execution agents cooperate.
Using these advanced features required "large amounts of architecture-specific orchestration code", as they were not readily available as Triton compilers abstractions. To address this challenge, Meta developed Triton Low-Level Extensions (TLX), designed to give engineers explicit control over GPU execution while preserving Triton's programming model.

articles.title: Super-hot rock geothermal could end data center energy woes | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Geothermal startups are in a race to see who can tap the deepest, hottest rocks. The winners could power the next phase of the grid, data centers and all.
The broader markets got their first taste of enhanced geothermal earlier this year when Fervo Energy went public. But this week was all about super-hot rock geothermal.
Geothermal has become a darling among investors, tech companies, and even the Trump administration. The basic technology has been around for decades, but advances in drilling techniques borrowed from the oil and gas industry has supercharged it. The U.S. has plenty of potential, too, with up to 57 terawatts of generating capacity, more than enough to power the next wave of AI data centers.
An emerging class of geothermal energy, known as super-hot rock, could help the industry unlock much of that potential.
The secret to super-hot rock geothermal is what happens to water at extreme depths. As it gets closer to the superheated core of the Earth, both temperature and pressure rise significantly. When they get high enough, ordinary water turns into a supercritical fluid — a sort of gaseous-liquid state that can carry tremendous amounts of energy. A single super-hot rock well could generate 15 megawatts of electricity or more.

Googles Gemini kann bald Macs steuern: Was die KI für Nutzer erledigen soll
Mac-User:innen in den USA, die Gemini nutzen, dürfen sich über weitere Features freuen. Google stattet die KI mit der Fertigkeit aus, die Steuerung der Apple-Computer zu übernehmen. Wie das Unternehmen in einem ausführlichen Blog-Beitrag schreibt, soll Gemini dabei repetitive Aufgaben von User:innen übernehmen, die sie nicht mehr erledigen möchten.
Was Gemini auf Macs machen kann
Laut Google kann Gemini auf Macs dabei auf lokale Dateien, Desktop-Apps und das Web zugreifen. Sobald eine Aufgabe erteilt wurde, läuft die KI in einem isolierten Hintergrundfenster weiter. Alle Handlungen werden in einer Live-Preview im Chat angezeigt. Dadurch können Mac-User:innen problemlos andere Dinge auf ihrem Gerät erledigen, während Gemini im Hintergrund die Aufgaben abhakt.
Um besser zu verstehen, was Gemini für User:innen erledigen kann, gibt Google einige Beispiele. So kann die KI etwa mehrere Fotos nacheinander mit einer bestimmten Software bearbeiten oder Informationen aus PDF-Dateien extrahieren und sie in andere Formulare eintragen. The world’s richest man has outlined ambitious plans to power AI models with data centers cooled by the vacuum of space. That will require packing satellites full of advanced chips.
SpaceX has said it plans to use the chips involved in the debt deal on Earth. But lenders have expressed concerns that if the group later decided to shoot the valuable chips that underpin their loans into space, it would prevent them from reclaiming and selling the semiconductors in the event of a default, according to people familiar with the matter.
It is uncertain whether the provision was included in the finalized documents.
The bonds were issued by a special purpose vehicle designed to keep the debt off SpaceX’s balance sheet and preserve its investment-grade credit rating.
The proposed debt covenant presented potential legal challenges for SpaceX’s ambitions to build data centers in space, highlighting the uncharted territory that investors need to navigate when financing the nascent asset class.
SpaceX sold more than $30 billion of the debt to large investors on Thursday as part of a financing package dubbed “Project Saturn.” The largest portion of the debt package was a $25 billion investment-grade bond backed by SpaceX’s five-year lease payment for the Nvidia chips.

articles.title: There are now more satellites over most towns than stars you can actually see
articles.summary:
The big picture: Light pollution has already whittled the night sky over most big cities down to a few dozen stars – maybe a few hundred out in the suburbs. Now, something else up there outnumbers them. A new analysis estimates that roughly 710 satellites sit above the horizon over a typical town at any given moment after dark.
Those figures come from The Night Sky Report, which UK engineering firm Accu Components published based on US Space Force tracking data from CelesTrak. The company plotted where nearly 15,900 active satellites in low Earth orbit sat every two minutes across seven October nights. Over a full night, it found that almost 13,000 different satellites pass over an average UK town.
Most of those can't actually be seen, though. Satellites have no lights of their own, so they only show up while sunlight still reaches them and the ground below has gone dark. The report puts that number at about 105 at any given moment – still more than the handful of stars most city dwellers can pick out.
That average hides a big swing across the night, too. A company spokesperson told Space.com that roughly 300 satellites catch the light in the first hour or so after dark. By midnight, fewer than 20 are still lit.
Weirdly, latitude works in opposite directions on each side of the Atlantic. In the UK, satellites thin out the farther north you go, so Lerwick in the Shetland Islands sees just 47 satellites high in the sky – more than 30 degrees up – compared to 83 in Falmouth. Acr…

Damals waren es 21,5 Prozent. Die typischsten Funde, gerade bei älteren Fahrzeugen, sind Mängel am Abblendlicht oder der hinteren Beleuchtung. Dazu kommen Ölverluste beim Motor oder Getriebe, Schäden an der Achsaufhängung und nicht mehr verkehrstaugliche Bremsscheiben.
Laut TÜV gelten diese Mängel sowohl bei Verbrennern als auch E-Autos. Bei elektrischen Fahrzeugen stehen aber meist die Bremsen an erster Stelle der Mängel. Neither design has a product name, a named controller or a sample date yet.
Phison detailed two new enterprise SSD designs at Supercomputer 2026 (SC26) that aim to answer two separate problems: one with a built-in NPU and 64GB of 130 GB/s memory that supports running PyTorch, vLLM, OpenVINO, and llama.cpp directly on the drive, and another that merges fast pSLC cache with large QLC capacity behind just one controller. The company notes that “many of the products and features mentioned are still in development” and will arrive once finalized.
The computational-storage design’s premise is that a server can offload more to the SSD, which runs AI code on the data where it already resides and sends back results, instead of whole datasets. The pSLC-QLC design, meanwhile, puts the cache inside each drive, which may reduce system complexity, as every drive bay contributes usable capacity and none goes to dedicated cache drives.
Phison says that the integrated NPU is expected to deliver “36,800 DMIPS of compute performance,” or Dhrystone Million Instructions Per Second, a typical synthetic benchmark. En los últimos meses Kirtsen Schwalbe ha salido del anonimato para protagonizar, casi en tiempo récord, un programa de telerrealidad, un libro biográfico y (en último lugar) una espinosa polémica que está sacudiendo su patria, Dinamarca. El motivo es simple: el país escandinavo acaba de descubrir que Schwalbe, de 112 años, su vecina más vetusta, tiene un pasado nazi.
La polémica está servida.
¿Quién es Kirsten Schwalbe? Si hicieses esa pregunta hace unas semanas la respuesta sería sencilla: ‘la abuela de Dinamarca’. El 14 octubre la mujer cumplió 112 años y 218 días, lo que la convierte en la danesa más longeva de la historia.
Nunca, desde que hay registros oficiales, un ciudadano danés había vivido tanto. El récord anterior lo tenía Karla Lindholm Jensen, fallecida en 2020 con 112 años y 217 días. La longevidad de Schwalbe parece ser cosa de familia. Su hermano menor, Bertel, hace tiempo también que superó la centuria (104 años).
¿Cuál es su historia? Eso es lo que quisieron averiguar Frederik Helms y Line Morell Holm, los autores de una biografía sobre Schwalbe publicada hace poco por la editorial danesa Gyldendal. La obra se tituló ‘Necesitamos algo de lo que reírnos’ y en la portada se mostraba a la propia Schwalbe, sonriente.
El problema es que la publicación despertó la curiosidad de varios periodistas e historiadores que, más allá de lo que contaba el libro, decidieron bucear por su cuenta en los archivos. Su objetivo: conocer más detalles de Schwalbe.

articles.title: Orphelin de Jensen Huang, Nvidia fait les yeux doux au patron d’un autre géant des puces
articles.summary:
La démission de Jensen Huang, le 12 novembre, a laissé Nvidia sans capitaine attitré pour la première fois en 33 ans d’existence. Le conseil d’administration a confié l’intérim à la directrice financière Colette Kress, le temps de trouver un successeur permanent. Les chasseurs de têtes mandatés pour l’occasion auraient déjà pris contact avec Rene Haas, le directeur général d’Arm.
Un candidat formé par Jensen Huang lui-même
Rene Haas a passé sept ans chez Nvidia, de 2006 à 2013, comme directeur général des produits de calcul, l’une des principales sources de revenus du groupe, sous les ordres directs de Jensen Huang. Parti chez Arm en 2013, il a dirigé l’activité de licences avant de prendre la tête du concepteur de puces britannique en 2022. Il entretiendrait toujours des liens étroits avec son ancien mentor et avec plusieurs administrateurs de Nvidia.
Le conseil l’aurait sondé dès le 13 novembre, au lendemain de l’annonce du départ, et l’action Arm a plongé de près de 10 % en séance après ces révélations. Le cabinet Heidrick & Struggles, recruté pour piloter la succession, a pris le relais le 18 novembre en contactant l’intéressé, ainsi que d’autres dirigeants susceptibles d’entrer dans la course. Haas figure parmi plusieurs profils étudiés, sans garantie qu’une offre lui soit adressée ni qu’il l’accepte. D’autres noms circulent, comme Ian Buck, vice-président de Nvidia, Lisa Su, patronne d’AMD, ou Johny Srouji, responsable des puces d’Apple.

Paid for an ExpressVPN auto-renewal you didn't want? Californians may be owed up to double that sum
California subscribers hit with ExpressVPN auto-renewal charges between 2022 and 2025 have until January 12, 2027 to file a claim
- ExpressVPN agreed to pay $3.9M to settle a California auto-renewal lawsuit
- Eligible subscribers can claim up to double the charge
- The window to raise the claim closes on January 12, 2027
California residents who were automatically billed for ExpressVPN between September 15, 2022, and June 13, 2025 can now apply for a payout from a $3.9 million class action settlement.
Eligible claimants can request up to twice what they paid during that period, while former subscribers will also receive a three-month voucher.
The deal resolves Marin et al. v. Express Technologies, Ltd. in San Diego County Superior Court.
While ExpressVPN remains near the top of our best VPN rankings for security and streaming, its subscription billing has faced legal scrutiny alongside rivals NordVPN and Surfshark.
Users outside California cannot claim from this fund, and payouts are not guaranteed yet. A judge must still grant final approval at a hearing scheduled for February 19, 2027.

Quebecor says a Bell-Telus merger wouldn’t be “a positive outcome for consumers” amid its own efforts to buy Telus and consolidate Canada’s telecom industry.
The company published a release railing against a possible Bell-Telus merger after reports that the companies engaged in preliminary talks. Those talks came in response to Quebecor’s own push to acquire Telus.

“Year after year, the company ranks among the telecommunications providers generating the highest number of complaints filed with the Commission for Complaints for Telecom-television Services (CCTS),” Quebecor argued.
Quebecor also touched on Bell and Telus’ fight with the CRTC over the junk fee ban, implying that a merger between the two would only increase these practices.
Elsewhere, Quebecor doubled down on its argument that a Quebecor-Telus merger would help the companies better combat foreign players.
“The interest successively shown by Quebecor and then Bell in Telus points to the same reality: Canada’s telecommunications sector must be strengthened, particularly in the face of new American technology and satellite players,” the company said in the press release. “Canada needs strong companies that can invest at scale while remaining under Canadian control.”

articles.title: Exclusive: Daniel Ek backs AI researcher's fusion power startup. Here's what they're building. | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Spotify founder Daniel Ek is backing Europa Fusion, a stealthy fusion power startup founded by an AI researcher who is taking a different approach to developing a fusion power plant.
The U.K.-based startup was founded in February, though sources told TechCrunch that the founder, Nantas Nardelli, has been working on the idea for longer. The people asked not to be identified because the information isn’t public. Bloomberg first reported Ek’s backing of Europa Fusion.
Nardelli has extensive experience in the AI world, having previously worked at Google DeepMind, Facebook AI Research, and Microsoft Research Cambridge. Recently, he was head of machine learning at Pacific Fusion, the fusion power startup based in Fremont, California.
Pacific Fusion recently broke ground on a demonstration facility in New Mexico. Like most fusion startups of its size, Pacific Fusion leans heavily on physical devices to test its theories and improve its simulations.
Nardelli apparently didn’t agree with the focus on hardware, instead thinking that fusion startups should invest in a more simulation- and data-heavy approach, a source familiar with his thinking told TechCrunch.
Like Pacific Fusion, Europa Fusion will pursue a pulsed-power approach to fusion. Pulsed-power reactors use massive, perfectly timed surges of electrical current to compress fuel targets until the atoms inside fuse and release energy.

articles.title: Cómo activar en el iPhone la protección que frena a un ladrón que conoce el código de acceso
articles.summary:
Si alguien roba un iPhone y conoce su código de desbloqueo, puede cambiar la clave de la cuenta de Apple y dejar al dueño sin acceso. La Protección de dispositivo robado lo impide: exige Face ID o Touch ID y una espera de una hora. Apple aclara que debe activarse antes del robo.
La función está disponible desde iOS 17.3, según la página de soporte de la empresa, actualizada el 22 de octubre de 2026. Apple indica que puede venir encendida de fábrica, pero conviene comprobarlo en los ajustes, porque si el teléfono ya fue robado no se puede activar.
Cómo activarla paso a paso
Para encenderla hace falta usar la verificación en dos pasos de la cuenta de Apple y tener configurados un código de desbloqueo, Face ID o Touch ID, y la opción Ubicaciones importantes dentro de los servicios de localización. También debe estar activo Buscar (Find My), que no se puede apagar mientras la protección funcione.
Los pasos, según la guía del usuario del iPhone:
- Entrar en Ajustes y tocar Face ID y código (en un iPhone SE, Touch ID y código).
- Escribir el código del teléfono.
- Bajar hasta Protección de dispositivo robado.
- Encender el interruptor.
Si el menú no aparece, Apple recomienda configurar antes Face ID o Touch ID. Al encender la función, el sistema pide elegir entre dos modos: usarla solo lejos de casa o del trabajo, o en todo lugar con la opción Siempre. Hackerangriff auf Kühlschränke vereitelt: So schützte Großbritannien Zehntausende Geräte vor fremden Zugriffen
Mitte Oktober 2026 kam es in Europa zu mehreren Cyberangriffen, die aber von klassischen Hackerattacken abwichen. Statt Servern und Computern nahmen die Angreifer smarte Kühlschränke von Supermärkten ins Visier. Sie manipulierten die Geräte so, dass Lebensmittel verdarben und Preise an den digitalen Schildern nicht mehr korrekt angezeigt werden konnten. Und jetzt haben britische Behörden Vorsichtsmaßnahmen ergriffen, um solche Attacken im eigenen Land zu verhindern.
Cybersecurity bei Kühlschränken: So sind britische Behörden vorgegangen
Das geht aus einem Bericht der BBC hervor, der absichtlich für eine gewisse Zeit zurückgehalten wurde. So sollte sichergestellt werden, dass potenzielle Schwachstellen in Kühlschränken in Großbritannien behoben werden können, bevor Hacker:innen die Lücken ausnutzen. Die Lücke wurde laut BBC von Omega Solutions, einem Beratungsunternehmen für Kühlschränke, entdeckt.
Ein Mitarbeiter soll einen genaueren Blick auf die Sicherheitsaspekte der meistverkauften Kühlschrank-Controller geworfen haben. Diese werden von der Firma Resource Data Manager entwickelt. Auslöser für die Untersuchung waren die vorherigen Angriffe auf andere Hersteller. Dabei entdeckte der Omega-Solutions-Mitarbeiter eine kritische Schwachstelle in den Controllern.

Les “unified plans” forment un système unique pour suivre ses tâches seul, en équipe ou à l’échelle d’une organisation. Il réunit les fonctions de To Do et des plans Planner Basic et Premium sur une même base.
Planner prend la suite de To Do, mais seulement au bureau

Les comptes professionnels et scolaires auront une page « My tasks » repensée dès décembre. Côté technique, les outils d’IA comme le Planner Agent ne fonctionnent qu’avec ces plans. C’est aussi le cas du Planner MCP server, une porte d’entrée standard qui permet à des agents d'IA de lire et de modifier les tâches. Les plans Premium, qui reposent sur Dataverse (le service de stockage de données de Microsoft), ne reçoivent plus de nouveautés.
Pour les comptes Microsoft personnels, Planner n’est tout simplement pas proposé. Microsoft promet un outil d’export, mais n’a publié aucune instruction. Un export ne garantit d’ailleurs pas une importation ailleurs. Les tâches existantes ne sont pas migrées. articles.title: Samsung agora permite bloquear apps individualmente nos celulares • Tecnoblog

Samsung agora permite bloquear apps individualmente nos celulares
Recurso da One UI 9.5 protege aplicativos com biometria, PIN, senha ou padrão e começa a chegar aos Galaxy S26.
A nova atualização da Samsung deve facilitar a vida de quem quer dificultar o acesso de possíveis enxeridos a informações privadas. A companhia começou a liberar, na One UI 9.5, um recurso nativo para bloquear aplicativos individualmente nos celulares da marca.
O recurso estreou no programa Beta do sistema operacional na linha Galaxy S26, e deve chegar posteriormente aos demais aparelhos compatíveis, segundo o site SamMobile.
O novo App Lock exige a mesma forma de autenticação usada para desbloquear o celular. Isso pode ser útil, por exemplo, quando o usuário entrega o aparelho já desbloqueado para outra pessoa, mas não quer permitir o acesso a aplicativos de mensagens, bancos, fotos ou outros serviços pessoais.
A proteção também se aplica às notificações dos aplicativos, que são ocultadas. Widgets dos aplicativos também desaparecem da tela inicial quando a trava é ativada.

articles.title: VAST Data says petabyte SSDs will outgrow RAID in today’s parallel file systems
articles.summary:
VAST Data says petabyte SSDs will outgrow RAID in today’s parallel file systems — simulation of a 900 PB system puts data-loss odds at 1 in 11 over 10 years
Built from 15 TB drives, VAST’s 900 PB system would draw about 5.6 MW instead of 400 kW.
VAST Data says petabyte SSDs will outgrow RAID in today’s parallel file systems, according to a simulation of its own 900 PB system that puts the odds of data loss at 1 in 11 over 10 years. At Supercomputing 2026 (SC26), the company explains how.
Bigger drives take longer to rebuild after a failure, leaving more time for further failures to lose data, but operators will still want those large drives because many sites are power-constrained and storage power scales with bandwidth rather than capacity. VAST’s recommended fix: system-wide erasure coding with at least three parity strips.
The company’s principal technical strategist, Glenn Lockwood, walked through the simulation, described as a “discrete event simulation” using real failure data, in an Exhibitor Forum talk during SC26’s HPC System Hardware and Architecture session. With petabyte-scale SSDs swapped in, enclosure-local declustered RAID — the approach used by DDN EXAScaler and HPE Cray ClusterStor, per Lockwood — has those exceptionally high odds of data loss. With global declustering and extra parity, operators can get this down to 1 in 54 million, a significant improvement, but VAST’s own scheme gets to about 1 in 62 billion, three orders of magnitude better.

articles.title: GTA VI has already broken internet usage records
articles.summary:
Grand Theft Auto VI is expected to break sales records, but it’s already breaking internet usage records as well.
As reported by internet infrastructure company DE-CIX, downloads going through its network on Nov. 18, the evening before the game’s launch, surpassed 33.03 terabits per second.
For context, this works out to 13 copies of the game per second and 25 percent higher data transfer and usage than during a typical week at the beginning of the year. Various internet service providers (ISPs) around the world have also been reporting massive GTA-driven spikes.
This isn’t exactly surprising, given that GTA VI is a digital-only, 200-plus gigabyte title, but it does speak to the sheer raw demand for the open-world crime game.
On the economic front, the game is also projected to have already earned more than US$2 billion. To put that into perspective, the highest-grossing movie of all time, Avengers: Endgame, sits just shy of $3 billion in lifetime gross.
It’s also important to stress that the game is only available on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. We still don’t have dates for the game’s inevitable PC port and GTA Online components. Naturally, those will only drive even more people to GTA VI.
Are you playing GTA VI? Let us know in the comments.

Na bitte, geht doch, könnte man nach dem Gezerre um die Stromsteuer sagen. Die Koalition hat in einer stundenlangen Sitzung beschlossen, die Stromsteuer auch für Privathaushalte auf das europäische Mindestmaß zu senken. Für Unternehmen gilt eine solche Regelung schon länger.
Dass ein durchschnittlicher Haushalt dadurch lediglich vier bis acht Euro im Monat sparen wird – geschenkt. In diesem Fall ist schon die Geste viel wert. Alles andere wäre nämlich ein Desaster gewesen: für Friedrich Merz persönlich (er hatte die Senkung gefordert), für die Glaubwürdigkeit der Koalition (die Senkung wurde im Koalitionsvertrag versprochen) und für die gesamte Energiewende sowieso (Elektrifizierung ist ein entscheidender Hebel zur Senkung der Emissionen).
Stromsteuer-Senkung ist mehr ein Provisorium als gesichert
Doch die Koalition wäre nicht die Koalition, wenn sie nicht an entscheidender Stelle wieder nur ein halbgares und halbherziges Provisorium angerichtet hätte. Die Steuersenkung ist nämlich nur auf das Jahr 2027 befristet. Alles darüber hinaus steht unter Finanzierungsvorbehalt.
Man darf sich also darauf einstellen, dass das einmal Erreichte bei jeder neuen Haushaltsverhandlung wieder infragegestellt wird. Dabei sehnen sich Unternehmen und Privatpersonen vor allem nach Planungssicherheit. Proposed in 1859 by Bernhard Riemann, who gave the problem its name, it is the theory that prime numbers are not in fact random but determined. "The Riemann hypothesis asserts that all interesting solutions of the equation ζ(s) = 0 lie on a certain vertical straight line," the Clay Mathematics Institute explains. articles.title: Scientists modify standard 3D printer to build 100-layer structures using living bacteria
articles.summary:
In context: In many ways, a bioprinter is simply a 3D printer that extrudes gels containing living cells instead of molten plastic. Commercial models can easily cost more than $100,000, however, prompting some labs to convert inexpensive hobbyist 3D printers into bioprinters themselves. But because the soft gel tends to sag before it solidifies, most of these DIY machines have been limited to printing fewer than 20 layers.
Now, a team from the University of Rochester and Cornell University has built one capable of stacking around 100 layers, all for about $450. In a study published in ACS Applied Polymer Materials, the researchers describe how they started with a standard Creality Ender 3 and replaced its print head with a syringe pump held together by 3D-printed PETG components.
The pump doesn't just push ink out, either. It can also pull it back between movements, much like the retraction setting Ender owners adjust to prevent stringing. Fine-tuning these movements reduced stray bacterial deposits by nearly 100-fold. As a result, the setup can print what lead researcher Anne Meyer describes as "crisp shapes with well-defined edges."
The extra height, however, comes from where the ink is deposited. Rather than printing on a bare build plate, the nozzle operates inside a slurry made of tiny gelatin or agarose particles mixed with calcium chloride. Amortiguan caídas, evitan que los niños se rompan un hueso y dan una segunda vida a millones de ruedas usadas. Sin embargo, hay un debate de fondo sobre si estas superficies pueden afectar a la salud de los más pequeños por su contenido en metales pesados.
¿Cuándo es peligroso? En toxicología y salud ambiental existe una regla de oro que pasa por decir que el peligro no es sinónimo de riesgo. En otras palabras, que un material contenga una sustancia potencialmente tóxica en su interior no significa que esta vaya a liberarse, entrar en el organismo humano y alcanzar la dosis necesaria para causar un daño. articles.summary:
Friday, November 20th 2026
Microsoft Brings RDMA over USB4 to Windows 11 for Daisy-Chained PCs
Microsoft is finally enabling Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) over the USB4 protocol on Windows 11, allowing multiple PCs to be daisy-chained and used together to process large workloads. This means that Windows 11 now has a mechanism to distribute a workload across multiple interconnected PCs, enabling faster processing. Essentially, AI inferencing at home is now limited by the number of PCs and their specifications, rather than a single PC. RDMA allows the workload to directly access system memory on another PC, all through USB4, which offers up to 80 Gbps bandwidth for fast data transfer.
Instead of using Ethernet over USB4 in a UDP packet configuration, Microsoft chose to implement RDMA over USB4 to significantly reduce data access latency. Microsoft interconnected two PCs to measure round-trip latency by message size, finding that RDMA over USB4 achieves latency between 28 and 50 microseconds. In contrast, Ethernet over USB4 using UDP results in latency between 116 and 194 microseconds, making the RDMA implementation roughly four times faster. This lower latency will greatly benefit systems running large workloads, especially in latency-sensitive tasks like AI inferencing. articles.title: AI Server Boards Are Now Draining the PCB Supply Chain
articles.summary:
Friday, November 20th 2026
AI Server Boards Are Now Draining the PCB Supply Chain
If there was one humble component relatively safe from the component crisis brought about by the AI boom, it was the PCB. However, it looks like that is no longer the case. The Global Electronics Association, formerly known as IPC, issued a new industry alert warning that AI servers are soaking up board capacity and materials at an alarming rate. PCB bookings in North America are reportedly up 56.1% this year through September, while shipments have grown just 13.3%. The group thinks this shortage could rival the 2021 chip crisis, as lead times for high-layer boards are 16 to 20 weeks, or even more. Companies in the automotive, industrial, defense, medical, and telecom sectors are reportedly struggling to secure enough supply. As a result, the association sees availability as a bigger risk than supply.
The reasoning behind their concern is also quite interesting. A typical PCB has around 12 layers, while AI server boards are moving to 40 to 60 layers or more. Each extra layer uses more glass fabric, resin, copper foil, laminate, and other raw materials. The industry is trying to expand to match the demand, with at least $10 billion going into PCB plants in Southeast Asia and China over the past three years. However, the raw materials themselves are in short supply, and hyperscalers have their eyes on that limited supply too. Last month, we reported that some PCB orders were taking up to 30 months…

El valor de la criptomoneda ethereum para este día a las 14:05 horas (UTC) es de 1731.72 dólares. Esto quiere decir que la moneda digital registró un cambio de -3.92% en el último día, así como un movimiento de 0.0% en la última hora.

Cotización de la criptomoneda Ethereum

Según The New York Times, la franquicia funciona como un collage de referencias culturales que Estados Unidos exportó durante décadas a través del cine, la música y la televisión. El resultado es una ciudad virtual que no reproduce la realidad estadounidense, sino la imagen que ese país proyectó hacia afuera, llevada al extremo.
Grand Theft Auto no comenzó con desarrolladores estadounidenses, ni siquiera con muchos de ellos. La primera entrega se gestó en Escocia y se lanzó en 1997, después de que sus creadores alimentaran de manera intencional una polémica mediática en el Reino Unido en torno a su contenido vulgar. La estrategia funcionó: las ventas crecieron y las secuelas se multiplicaron en los años siguientes. Rockstar Games, el estudio que hoy desarrolla la franquicia, acumula cientos de millones de copias vendidas y ganancias extraordinarias.

Researchers planted 2 million digital tripwires in requests sent through a sprawling network of AI services to find out what happened to sensitive information entrusted to them. What they discovered was an ecosystem that leaked highly sensitive data like a sieve.
The exposure was found through an ingenious experiment designed to test if sensitive information can leak through the vast chain of widely used AI services and how that information is exploited when it does. Many of today’s AI apps use services such as OpenRouter or Vercel that act as brokers. These “AI routers,” sometimes also known as “AI gateways,” receive large numbers of prompts sent from AI app end users and route them to an available inference engine based on criteria such as the one charging the lowest price or being best suited for the given task. Instead of using Anthropic, OpenAI, or another big provider, the developer hires an AI router to find the most suitable model.
Security breaches, prompt theft, and privacy violations
To test for potential leakage, researcher HD Moore assembled a collection of AWS access keys, functioning credentials tied to empty AWS accounts, passwords for services such as SSH, and unique URLs, DNS names, and private git repository references. None of the secrets had ever been used before, and he controlled the infrastructure that received any requests using the credentials. Avec plus de temps, il espère aussi venir à bout de l'hypothèse de Riemann "étendue".
Formulée en 1859 par l'Allemand Bernhard Riemann, la conjecture affirme que les zéros dits "non triviaux" de la fonction zêta s'alignent tous sur une même droite. Les équipes de l’ESA ont donc fait tourner, année après année, les moteurs électriques du module de transfert. articles.title: Qué significa Grand Theft Auto, cómo se pronuncia y qué significa GTA
articles.summary:
Grand Theft Auto significa, en términos generales, “robo de automóvil” dentro de una categoría legal de robo agravado. Es una expresión del inglés estadounidense que da nombre a la saga de videojuegos de Rockstar. Sus iniciales forman GTA, la abreviatura por la que millones de personas conocen la franquicia.
La traducción palabra por palabra puede confundir. “Grand” significa “grande” en muchos contextos, pero en esta expresión no describe el tamaño del auto ni necesariamente un robo espectacular. “Grand theft” es un término legal para una forma grave de hurto o robo; “auto” se refiere al automóvil. Por eso, una traducción más clara sería “robo agravado de automóvil”, aunque la equivalencia exacta depende de las leyes de cada lugar.
En California, por ejemplo, el Código Penal incluye el robo de un automóvil dentro de las circunstancias que pueden constituir grand theft. Las definiciones y sanciones cambian según la jurisdicción, por lo que la expresión no tiene una aplicación idéntica en todo Estados Unidos.
Cómo se pronuncia Grand Theft Auto
En inglés estadounidense, la pronunciación aproximada es “grand eft áuto”. La primera palabra suena parecido a “grand”, pero la vocal de grand se pronuncia entre una “a” y una “e”. En theft, el sonido inicial th se produce colocando suavemente la lengua entre los dientes y dejando salir el aire, como en la palabra inglesa think. No suena exactamente como la “z” de España ni como la “s” que suele usarse en América Latina.

A newly disclosed unpatched zero-day technique called FastUnlock lets someone with physical access to a locked Windows computer start programs without signing in. Whoever uses it gets only a limited account, not administrator control of the machine.
The method was posted yesterday by a researcher who uses the handles MSNightmare and Nightmare Eclipse, and the endpoint-security firm ThreatLocker tested it the same day and found it works.
There is no fix from Microsoft yet, and nothing shows the method has been used in a real attack.
The technique does not work on every machine. It requires physical access to the computer and a Microsoft account accessible through the lock screen's recovery options, and it uses Windows' built-in screen reader, Narrator, to navigate the locked screen.
In its test, the firm reached a point where it could run a program from the lock screen in a limited account that ThreatLocker identified as WSIAccount and said is "not an administrator account."
The researcher's GitHub disclosure is a short post with a video and little written detail, so the clearest account of what the flaw does comes from the firm's independent test.
Many Windows computers encrypt their drives with BitLocker, but in a common setup, that does not make them immune to this technique. articles.title: Watching as a giant star swallowed its neighbor and exploded
articles.summary:
In the Andromeda Galaxy, a giant star about seven times as massive as the Sun spent nearly a decade slowly swallowing its much smaller companion. The process, known as common envelope evolution, was proposed in the 1970s to explain how some of the tightest pairs of stars in the Universe form, but no one had ever caught it in the act.
In a new Nature study, astronomers led by Viraj Karambelkar, an astrophysicist at Columbia University, finally witnessed the entire spectacle from the decades before it began to the eruption that ended it in late 2025. “It lasts for a few years, maybe a few decades,” Karambelkar said. “Stars evolve on time scales of millions of years. So, it’s really like a blip on the entire cosmic time scale.”
Shared envelopes
Some pairs of stars orbit so close to each other that they could not have formed at that distance, so their orbits must have shrunk. Common envelope evolution is the leading explanation for that shrinkage. When one star in a binary grows old, it expands into a giant, and its outer layers can engulf its companion. The two then share a single, loosely bound envelope of gas. As the engulfed star drags through it, it loses orbital energy to friction and spirals inward. Depending on how much of the envelope gets lost, the pair either ends up in a much tighter orbit or merges.

articles.title: Por qué una caída digital afecta pagos, llamadas y aplicaciones al mismo tiempo

La causa puede estar fuera de la pantalla: una conexión compartida, un corte de electricidad o un sistema que confirma la identidad del usuario pueden interrumpir varias actividades a la vez.
Una dependencia compartida puede afectar servicios distintos
Una dependencia existe cuando un servicio necesita recursos de otro para funcionar. La CISA, agencia de Estados Unidos dedicada a la seguridad de infraestructuras, distingue cuatro tipos de dependencia: física, cuando requiere electricidad; geográfica, cuando varios recursos quedan expuestos al mismo hecho local; cibernética, cuando depende de datos o sistemas ajenos; y lógica, cuando la relación surge de decisiones, normas o procedimientos. Un problema en uno de esos puntos puede interrumpir otras funciones conectadas.
Una plataforma puede depender de la conexión a internet, del almacenamiento remoto de información, de la energía eléctrica y de un sistema de acceso. Por eso, dos empresas con aplicaciones diferentes pueden dejar de operar si usan el mismo proveedor o la misma red. Ese recurso común constituye un punto único de falla, es decir, un elemento cuya interrupción afecta a varios servicios.

Una llamada de un hijo, un nieto o un hermano que dice estar en problemas y pide dinero de inmediato puede ser una estafa con la voz del familiar copiada por inteligencia artificial. La Comisión Federal de Comercio (FTC) de Estados Unidos recomienda no confiar en la voz y verificar por otra vía.
El aviso más reciente de la FTC, publicado el 18 de noviembre, describe cómo funciona el engaño. El estafador llama y se hace pasar por alguien querido. Algunos usan herramientas digitales para crear videos falsos o clonar la voz del familiar, según la agencia.
La historia suele ser urgente: un arresto que exige fianza, una reparación de un auto, un accidente. El interlocutor pide dinero cuanto antes y agrega una condición: que la víctima no se lo cuente a nadie.
Qué hacer durante la llamada
La FTC indica tres pasos. El primero es ir más despacio: colgar o decir que se devolverá la llamada enseguida. Los estafadores buscan que la víctima se asuste y pague antes de tener tiempo de pensar o de consultar a alguien de confianza.
El segundo paso es llamar a otro familiar o a un amigo para comprobar si la historia es cierta. El tercero es no enviar dinero a quien exija un método de pago concreto: transferencia, criptomonedas, aplicación de pagos o tarjeta de regalo.
La Comisión Federal de Comunicaciones (FCC), el regulador de telecomunicaciones de Estados Unidos, agrega un detalle práctico en una alerta actualizada el 24 de abril. Después de colgar, hay que llamar al supuesto afectado al nú…

articles.title: Hackers Exploit Critical Cisco Expressway Flaw, Breach Four Devices and Reach Internal Network
articles.summary:
Threat actors have been observed exploiting a recently disclosed critical security flaw in Cisco Expressway to breach a Russian organization shortly after the public release of a proof-of-concept (PoC) exploit.
The activity involves the exploitation of CVE-2026-76466 (CVSS score: 9.8), a vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker with network access to a Cisco Expressway device to execute arbitrary operating system commands as root.
"This vulnerability is due to the use of persistent cookies," Cisco said in an advisory released late last month. "Additionally, there is insufficient validation of client certificates when the TLS Verify Mode is set to Enabled for clustering, which means that client certificates are not validated."
"An attacker with possession of the cookies could exploit this vulnerability by connecting to the database service and invoking specific remote procedure call (RPC) commands. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to execute arbitrary commands as root on the underlying operating system of an affected device."
Patches for the flaw were released in the following versions on October 21, 2026 -
- Cisco Expressway Series Release X14 and earlier - Migrate to a fixed release
- Cisco Expressway Series Release X15.5.3 and earlier - X15.5.20

articles.title: El MIT crea un método para mejorar detectores de textos realizados con IA que alcanza el 93% de precisión: cómo funciona
articles.summary:
Investigadores del Instituto de Tecnología de Massachusetts (MIT) y la Universidad Cornell demostraron que adaptar los detectores de texto generado por inteligencia artificial mientras analizan nuevos contenidos eleva al 93 % su capacidad para identificar escritos de IA diseñados para pasar como humanos, frente al 27 % que alcanzan los sistemas convencionales.
El hallazgo abre la puerta a herramientas más confiables para docentes, editores y expertos en ciberseguridad, aunque los propios autores advierten que podría no existir una solución definitiva, informó MIT News, el portal de noticias del instituto.
A diferencia de los métodos tradicionales, que requieren reentrenar el modelo desde cero ante cada cambio, el enfoque evaluado permite que el detector se actualice de forma continua a partir de los textos que recibe una vez puesto en funcionamiento, sin necesidad de conocer su origen. Esto lo hace más resistente tanto a los cambios naturales en los hábitos de escritura como a los intentos deliberados de evasión.
El estudio, publicado en arXiv, fue encabezado por Kevin Ren, estudiante de posgrado en Cornell Tech, junto con Nikhil Garg, profesor asistente de Cornell Tech, y Manish Raghavan, profesor de desarrollo profesional Drew Houston (2005) de la Escuela de Administración Sloan del MIT.

articles.title: The Path to AI Autonomy in the SOC
articles.summary:
Security leaders are about to hand AI agents a lot more authority. In a recent a16z survey of CISOs at organizations with more than 1,000 employees, 36% said they are comfortable today letting AI agents act autonomously on low-risk security actions. In 12 months from now, 60% expect to be comfortable at that level. Overall, AI SOC was the highest ranking initiative for 2027.
The pressure behind the shift is easy to see. In the same survey, the most common worry was AI-accelerated attacks outpacing the team's ability to respond, selected by 55% of respondents. Analyst time is the scarcest resource in the SOC, and every alert still means pulling evidence from several systems, reconstructing what happened and deciding whether it matters.
The same respondents are cautious at the top end. Only 1% are comfortable with agents acting autonomously on most actions today, and only 7% expect to be a year from now. Most teams want more autonomy, just not all of it.
Discussions today frame autonomy as a single slider that runs from "AI suggests" to "AI acts," and that exact framing is why so many programs stall. Autonomy is a set of decisions made per stage of the workflow and per action, and the teams that get it right treat it as something an agent earns with evidence.
Autonomy is not “all or nothing”, but rather a spectrum

articles.title: Linux KVM Flaw CVE-2026-99312 Lets Guest VMs Access Host Memory on AMD Hosts
articles.summary:
A flaw in KVM, the hypervisor built into the Linux kernel, let researchers read about 127 GB of a cloud server's memory from inside a virtual machine of their own on DigitalOcean.
On a shared server, that memory can include other customers' virtual machines. The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-99312, affects only hosts with AMD processors and nested virtualization enabled.
Fixed kernels shipped upstream on Tuesday, the day before the research went public. The provider patched its own fleet with a live patch, telling Droplet customers: "No action needed on your part." Operators who run their own KVM hosts on AMD hardware need to update the host kernel or turn nested virtualization off.
Oren Yomtov, a researcher at the security firm Terra Security, found the flaw and reported it through the provider's bug bounty program. The provider confirmed the exploit worked on its own hosts and treated it as critical, and the Linux KVM maintainers, told on October 21, merged a fix on November 2.
In the test on one of its Droplets, the first thing to come back was the host's kernel version banner, followed by about 127 GB of the host's RAM, mapped read-only, the provider said in a disclosure post yesterday.
The write test ran on the researchers' own bare-metal AMD server, with no other customers attached. There, the guest wrote 32 chosen bytes into a live page of the host kernel's memory, and a witness module loaded into that kernel confirmed the change.

articles.title: Bazuka Android Malware Uses Fake Screen Overlays to Hide Credential Theft and Device Control
articles.summary:
Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of a previously unknown Android malware framework called Bazuka that offers large language model (LLM) integration for victim management and control at scale.
Dutch mobile security company ThreatFabric said it discovered the threat in late October 2026 during an investigation into an NFC-relay banking Trojan.
"Bazuka is a full malware framework," ThreatFabric said in a technical report. "A dropper/downloader, a core, and 23 modules cover overlays, keylogging, 2FA and SMS interception, remote control, and crypto-address swapping."
One notable aspect of the malware that distinguishes it from the rest is a novel overlay technique that allows the trojan to take a screenshot of the home screen or lock screen, and display that as an overlay on demand to cover up malicious activities taking place in the background.
Another perhaps not-so-surprising element is the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in the control panel to help operators identify victims of interest and manage infections. It supports both locally hosted models and models accessed through an API.

articles.title: WhatsApp Patches 3 Security Flaws, Including Android Bug Suspected of Use in Scams
articles.summary:
Meta-owned WhatsApp has addressed security vulnerabilities, including one impacting its Android app that it suspects may have been exploited in connection with scam messages.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-23871, has been described as a case of incomplete validation of external ad-reply URLs in WhatsApp for Android and WhatsApp Business for Android before 2.26.17.4.
The issue could have "caused a target's device to reveal its IP information to an attacker if an attacker sent media from an attacker-controlled URL when a crafted Click to WhatsApp ad-reply message was rendered and displayed in a message thread," WhatsApp said.
The messaging platform said it may have been "abused in conjunction with specific spam messages." Internal researchers on the WhatsApp Security Team have been credited with discovering and reporting the issue.
When reached for comment, a WhatsApp spokesperson told The Hacker News that the vulnerability was discovered while disrupting a scam campaign. "We believe a scammer was using it to make their scam message seem more credible," the spokesperson added.
WhatsApp did not disclose the scale of the activity, and if those efforts were successful.
Also addressed by the company are two other flaws -

Le sous-marin nucléaire d'attaque De Grasse a été admis au service actif de la Marine nationale ce vendredi. Quatrième SNA de la classe Suffren, il peut désormais partir en mission, alors que la relève des Rubis entre dans sa dernière ligne droite.
C'est désormais officiel, le SNA De Grasse rejoint la flotte opérationnelle de la Marine nationale. L'amiral Christophe Cluzel, chef d'état-major de la Marine, a prononcé vendredi l'admission au service actif de ce sous-marin nucléaire d’attaque, livré par la Direction générale de l'armement (DGA) en juin après plusieurs mois d’essais en mer. Le bâtiment retrouve à Toulon ses trois aînés du programme Barracuda, tandis que les deux derniers exemplaires de la série se préparent encore à Cherbourg.
Feu vert pour le De Grasse, sentinelle silencieuse de la dissuasion nucléaire française
C'est sur ses réseaux sociaux que la Marine nationale a officialisé la nouvelle, ce vendredi 20 novembre. L'amiral Christophe Cluzel s'y dit « très heureux » d'avoir prononcé cette admission, avec, pour le De Grasse, l'incarnation des « ambitions d'une Marine de combat, avec des outils technologiquement à la pointe ». Le sous-marin, jusqu'ici en phase de test, peut désormais être envoyé en opération.
